item.title: Bears vs. Lions live updates, score: Colston Loveland carted to locker room with apparent lower-body injury
item.description: The Bears and Lions open up Thanksgiving football.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL is starting Thanksgiving off with a feast, with the top two teams in the NFC North facing off in the first game of the slate. The Detroit Lions and the Chicago Bears both enter Thursday's game 8-2 on multigame win streaks — and a chance to humble their rival on a national holiday.

The game also marks the return of Ben Johnson, who heads back to the Detroit for the second time since leaving the team to become Chicago's head coach. Johnson's Bears lost to the Lions twice last season, but the first meeting of the season between the two teams offers a chance for the former offensive coordinator to finally get that long-awaited win.

Detroit and Chicago are both offense-forward, especially on the ground, which should (hopefully) result in a high-scoring, high-velocity matchup. Expect plenty of highlights to devour alongside your turkey and mashed potatoes.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Bears and Lions kick off the Thanksgiving game slate in Week 12, airing on CBS and Paramount+.

item.title: Bears TE Colston Loveland carted into locker room, ruled out with knee injury
item.description: Loveland was taken into the medical tent in the first quarter of Chicago's Thanksgiving matchup against the Lions.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland has been ruled out with a knee injury after being carted into the locker room.

Loveland appeared to suffer the injury early in the Thanksgiving matchup against the Detroit Lions, and was taken into the medical tent in the first quarter. He was later transported to the locker room on the cart; the tight end, who put a towel over his head, was clearly emotional as he left the field.

Colston Loveland, with a towel over his head, is being carted to the #Bears locker room: pic.twitter.com/mzsASfgv5X

— Mason Williams (@mvsonwilliams) November 26, 2026

Shortly after the start of the second quarter, the Bears ruled Loveland out for the rest of the game with a knee injury.

#Bears TE Colston Loveland (Knee) has been ruled Out.

— Bears Communications (@BearsPR) November 26, 2026

Prior to the injury, Loveland had lost a fumble on Chicago’s opening drive, after the ball was punched out by Lions defensive end Derrick Moore. Detroit went three-and-out on the resulting drive, but later pulled to a 10-0 lead with a Jahmyr Gibbs touchdown to open the second quarter.

Loveland is a key piece of the Bears’ offense, with the third-most receiving yards on the team this season. Chicago already lost tight end Cole Kmet to a season-ending knee injury last month, leaving glaring holes in the Bears’ depth at tight end going forward.

This story will be updated.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs puts Lions up 10-0, Colston Loveland out with knee injury
item.description: Loveland left the game on a cart in the first quarter.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions are up two scores in the second quarter in Detroit.

Running back Jahmyr Gibbs punched the ball in from the 1-yard-line with 12:51 to play in the first half and the Lions are now up 10-0 on the Bears.

The Bears' comeback efforts will be hindered by the loss of tight end Colston Loveland. Loveland was carted off in the first quarter and the Lions announced that he is out for the rest of the game with a knee injury.

Gibbs is now up to 16 touchdowns on the season and he's picked up 55 yards from scrimmage thus far. Wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has three catches for 69 yards, including a 23-yarder on the touchdown drive.

Loveland lost a fumble on the Bears' first possession and the Lions forced a three-and-out on the second, so the offense needs to get in gear for Chicago.

item.title: Colston Loveland injury update: Bears TE ruled out with knee injury
item.description: The Bears standout tight end was injured in the first quarter vs. the Lions and had to be carted to the locker room.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland is off to a bad start to his Thanksgiving.

On Chicago's first possession of the game, Loveland's fumble in the red zone gave the ball back to the Detroit Lions. One possession later, the tight end had to be carted back to the locker room with an apparent lower body injury.

Loveland appeared to sustain his injury on the first play of the Bears' second offensive drive. While blocking a Lions defender on D'Andre Swift's short run up the middle, the tight end had his ankle rolled up on by Swift and Lions defensive tackle Tyleik Williams.

CBS cameras showed Loveland receiving attention from trainers on the sideline, and he was eventually carted back to the locker room.

Colston Loveland injury update

The Bears ruled Loveland out for the remainder of the Thanksgiving game against the Lions with a knee injury.

The second-year tight end appeared to sustain the ailment when his lower leg got rolled up on while he was making a block. One of Detroit's defensive lineman, Williams, tackled Swift, the Bears' running back, and both players got tangled up with Loveland, who was making a block.

Loveland had to be carted back to the locker room, and CBS sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson reported he was in tears.

What happened to Colston Loveland?

Loveland injured his knee in the first quarter of the Bears' clash with the Lions on Thanksgiving. Chicago has ruled the second-year tight end out of the game with his injury.

The injury appeared to occur on the first play of the Bears' second drive of the day. Loveland had to be carted off as a result.

item.title: Two former teammates slam Aaron Rodgers for Mike McCarthy comments
item.description: Former Packers players Greg Jennings and T.J. Lang criticized Aaron Rodgers for how he handled his Steelers departure.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Rodgers' scorched earth approach with Mike McCarthy was like the drop of a bomb. The fallout from its explosion has carried further than just the current Pittsburgh Steelers roster.

Former Green Bay Packers players from the Rodgers and McCarthy era – 2006 to 2018 – have started to weigh in on how the veteran quarterback handled his split from the Steelers. Greg Jennings, the wide receiver who spent seven years in Green Bay, and guard T.J. Lang, an eight-year Packer, both expressed their surprise at Rodgers' approach.

Neither player confirmed the quarterback's stories about McCarthy, and both had their criticisms for his explosive appearance on ESPN's "Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

AARON RODGERS: Veteran QB goes scorched earth on Mike McCarthy after Steelers benching

Rodgers' scathing comments about McCarthy came hours after the coach benched the quarterback in favor of Mason Rudolph late Tuesday, Nov. 24. In the aftermath of the "Pat McAfee Show" appearance, Pittsburgh waived the veteran quarterback ahead of Week 12.

Here's what Jennings and Lang said about Rodgers' comments:

Greg Jennings expresses shock, calls out A.J. Hawk

The former Packers wide receiver said he could not corroborate any of Rodgers' stories about McCarthy during the time they shared in Green Bay. He also noted his surprise at the lack of questions for A.J. Hawk, a former linebacker for the Packers who spent the 2006 through 2014 seasons in Green Bay and a mainstay on the "Pat McAfee Show."

"A large part of me just wanted someone to ask A.J., who was sitting right there, 'A.J., do you recall any of this stuff?' Please, someone, ask A.J., 'Can you confirm, or can you second any of this?'" Jennings said on FS1.

The former receiver said he also reached out to some of his other previous teammates in Green Bay, who also said they could not confirm any of Rodgers' stories about McCarthy.

Greg Jennings takes a shot at A.J. Hawk over Aaron Rodgers' 'McAfee Show' interview: "A large part of me just wanted someone to ask A.J., who was sitting right there, do you recall any of this stuff?" 🏈 📺 🧀 https://t.co/TDCzKtxMIn

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 25, 2026

T.J. Lang says Rodgers' approach was hypocritical

Lang, who spent the final two years of his career with the Lions, made an appearance on Detroit sports radio station 97.1 The Ticket on Wednesday, Nov. 25. He said Rodgers' decision to air out all of his grievances publicly was the exact kind of behavior the quarterback used to call out.

"I think it's despicable," Lang said. "I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has b----ed about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates. Airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media.

"He has blacklisted I don't know how many former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he was sick of it."

TJ Lang on his former teammate Aaron Rodgers https://t.co/0oiS3PybCn

— 97.1 The Ticket: (@971theticketxyt) November 25, 2026

The two-time Pro Bowler also cast doubt on some of Rodgers' comments, given that the Steelers chose to bench, then release the quarterback. Lang specifically called Rodgers out for saying he and Steelers general manager Omar Khan shared laughs about McCarthy's miscues as the head coach behind his back.

"Then why would Omar Khan side with Mike McCarthy? Why would Omar Khan allow Mike McCarthy to bench Aaron Rodgers and basically side with Mike McCarthy?" Lang said.

— 97.1 The Ticket: (@971theticketxyt) November 25, 2026

A key member of the Bears offense has gone to the locker room with an injury in the first quarter.

Tight end Colston Loveland was checked out in the sideline medical tent and then loaded onto a cart to head inside for further evaluations. Loveland had one catch for five yards, but then lost the ball on a hit by Lions defensive end Derrick Moore. Linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez recovered the ball to end the first Bears offensive possession of the day.

The Lions drove for a field goal to open the game and remain up 3-0 with under three minutes to play in the first quarter.

item.title: Packers By The Numbers: Stats from the Week 12 loss to the Rams
item.description: Digging into some numbers from the Packers Week 11 loss to the Rams
item.content:encoded:
As we do every week in this space, we’re looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers’ most recent game, courtesy of SumerSports. Today we’re looking at the 26-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in Week 12.

I don’t have metrics on the broadcast, but I can tell you with some amount of certainty that there was less dead air in this game than any other game this season. Luke Kuechly brought some really nice insight into some of the plays, but my goodness, fellas, you’re allowed to take a breath.

And stop trying to make “Thanksgiving Eve” happen. It’s not going to happen.

Offense

After leaning into a heavy personnel grouping last week, this week saw the Packers go back to primarily playing out of 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR).

And, lest you think the numbers are skewed due to a small number of plays in the second half (and needing to catch up when they did have the ball), those full game numbers are roughly in line with the first half approach.

They were primarily a shotgun-based passing attack offense in this game. For the game, they were in shotgun on 84.1% of snaps and had a pass rate of 68.2%. Again, those numbers basically align with the 1st half. They were 78.6% shotgun and 64.3% pass in the 1st half.

As we’ve seen them do all year, they switched up their run game approach in this game. After going with a power-heavy approach against the Vikings, they were back to a zone-based attack this week.

Inside Zone didn’t work overly well for them, but they did well with Outside Zone and Power. I’m curious to dig a little deeper into that when the film hits. Was that a matter of a smaller sample size, or was that something they could have leaned a bit heavier into if they wanted to?

Jordan Love had a pretty rough day in the stat sheet. He went 17/29 for 198 yards, 1 TD and 2 INTs for an EPA per Play of -0.31. That would go down as his worst game of the year by EPA per Play (behind the -0.22 he posted against the Vikings last week). As I mentioned at the top, I thought Kuechly did a nice job breaking down what Love was expecting on that 1st INT, and the second INT certainly seemed to be a case where Bo Melton cut off his route. So there are certainly things to consider (and things we’ll certainly be breaking down this week), but, right now, the numbers are the numbers and the numbers are bad.

Love did seem to have a little more time to throw in this game, but, as with every game this season, time is relative. The average time to pressure against Love was 2.3 seconds, 0.26 seconds below the NFL average. His average time to throw of 2.62 seconds seems downright functional, and would make this his 5th longest time to throw in a game this year. It’s still 0.08 seconds below the NFL average. So protection was better, but still below average. Still, it felt functional in a way it certainly did not against the Vikings.

Love came into this game shredding Man coverage, and the Rams came into the game playing one of the highest rates of man coverage in the league. Love continued playing well against man, but the zone stuff is ugly.

We don’t know how long Christian Watson will be out, but it sure would be nice if Tucker Kraft could find his game a little bit. He clearly is not all the way back from his injury (whether that’s physical or mental, I don’t really know), but the offense won’t really have a chance if he can’t find a way to turn it on.

Defense

Micah Parsons played limited snaps in his return to the field, but he was impactful while he was there, notching a 21.4% pressure rate and an average time to pressure of 2.47 seconds.

Parsons posted a pressure rate of 20.2% and an average time to pressure of 2.76 seconds last season, so he looked like Micah Parsons while he was on the field. That was certainly encouraging.

With Parsons back, I was certainly hoping for more from Lukas Van Ness, but we didn’t really see that. He had a pressure rate of 6.7% and an average time to pressure of 2.6 seconds. With as run-heavy as the Rams were (66.2% run rate for the game, 81.4% in the 2nd half) it’s hard to glean too much in terms of how the pass rush will look with Parsons back. Something to keep an eye on going forward.

Chris McClellan turned in a nice game with 4 assisted tackles, 4 solo tackles and 1 tackle for loss. I’m excited to take a look at him when the film comes out.

item.title: Packers Winners and Losers: Week 12 vs. the Rams
item.description: The best and worst as the Packers suffer their second straight loss.
item.content:encoded:
On Thanksgiving Eve, the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams faced off in a game which had heavy impact on the playoff chances for both teams. RG Kevin Zeitler made his first start for the Packers. EDGE Micah Parsons made his long awaited return after sustaining a torn ACL during the 2025 season. It was also another chapter in the Matt LaFleur vs. Sean McVay saga, and, for the first time since the two both became NFL head coaches, McVay and the Rams came out victorious, 26-13. Let’s take a look at what worked, and what didn’t.

Winner: Micah Parsons

It feels so good typing these words right now. After wondering what the heck was taking so long with the return of the Packers star edge rusher after a December 2025 ACL tear, it was revealed that the damage was much more severe than many of us realized. Last night, finally healthy, Parsons made his first start of the 2026 season, playing about 37% of total defensive snaps. And he looked…great!

Parsons nearly got to QB Matthew Stafford a few times, and then just before halftime, we all got to see the sack we’d been waiting 346 days for. With how things have been called all year for the Packers, I was certain this would be flagged for roughing the passer. Parsons finished the night with 1 sack and 2 QB hits, and was credited with 4 pressures on 26 snaps. Good stuff, and it’ll only get better.

Winner: Christian Watson

WR Christian Watson was the only reliable pass catcher for the Packers last night, and he was knocked out of the game in the first half after taking a nasty blow to the helmet, which saw Rams S Kam Kinchens ejected. Prior to the hit, Watson was the only one able to hold onto the ball or…do anything right, really. The routes were nice. The hands were strong. He finished the night catching all 4 targets for 65 yards and 1 TD. His concussion status will be one to monitor as the Packers head into their next game next Sunday.

Loser: Tucker Kraft

The Packers have had a problem with TE Tucker Kraft all season, and now, it’s got me begging them to stop giving him the ball. Kraft has had some pretty egregious drops this year, has played like he’s scared of getting hit, and has just been generally BAD. Last night, he logged his second fumble of the year, and the Rams were able to turn it into 3 more points. Kraft finished the night catching 3 of 5 targets for 24 yards. They don’t really have any other options at TE, so I guess we just hope for the best? And cry a little?

Loser: Matthew Golden

Last night was the first time I’ve seen QB Jordan Love visibly angry, and it came on the heels of an interception that seemed to have been caused by WR Matthew Golden running the wrong route. Golden has been great this year. He even showed flashes of that last night with his big 39 yard gain, but this error killed any sort of momentum the Packers were developing. Golden finished the night with 1 catch on 5 targets for 39 yards.

Loser: Bo Melton

It may not be a good idea to stop running and then just watch as the defender intercepts your quarterback.

Loser: Brian Gutekunst

We can blame the quarterback (not really), we can blame the offensive line, we can blame the receivers, we can blame the run defense, we can blame the head coach! At the end of the day, this goes back to GM Brian Gutekunst, who put the team together. Now—there are things he can’t control, like the drops, and the injury bug flying through the locker room. But the poor depth at offensive line has been the catalyst for almost all of the bad things to happen to the Packers offense this season.

Jordan Love has been running for his life. He’s being hit while throwing. The RB room doesn’t stand a chance. The receivers have had almost no time to get open. An even mediocre offensive line fixes a lot of this. By failing to put together an o-line group that can sustain any sort of run game, any sort of passing game other than “sling it and hope for the best”, Brian Gutekunst has bungled the 2026 roster.

The 6-5 Packers make their next appearance next Sunday, December 6, against the 3-7 New Orleans Saints. The game is at 1 pm ET/12 pm CT, and yes, that’s a threat.

item.title: NFL honors John Madden with Thanksgiving-themed coins, Madden uniform patch for Thursday slate
item.description: In the years since Madden's death in 2021, the league has continued to celebrate the broadcaster's connection to the holiday.
item.content:encoded:
Five years after the death of John Madden, the NFL is keeping the memory of the broadcaster's connection to Thanksgiving alive.

The league announced last week that a Madden coin, featuring Madden's silhouette on one side and a six-legged "turducken" (a chicken stuffed in a duck, stuffed in a turkey) on the other, will be used for coin flips for the three NFL games on Thanksgiving Day.

All players in those games — Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears, Dallas Cowboys-Philadelphia Eagles and Buffalo Bills-Kansas City Chiefs — will wear patches on their uniforms with the Madden silhouette. The Los Angeles Rams and Green Bay Packers, who played on Wednesday (or "Thanksgiving Eve," as the league calls it), also wore the patches.

Stencils honoring Madden will be placed in the end zones and along the sidelines of the three home fields during the matchup, and panels on the stadium wall will feature Madden in his coaching days with the Oakland Raiders.

Today’s NFL games will each feature an exclusive John Madden Thanksgiving-themed coin for the pregame coin flip 🪙

Teams will also wear a corresponding patch of Madden’s silhouette on their jerseys 👤 pic.twitter.com/CsK9COHVWc

— Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) November 26, 2026

Along with those Madden-themed additions, the MVP of each game will receive a trophy fashioned to look like a turkey leg-football amalgamation. The Thanksgiving MVPs will also earn a $10,000 donation from the NFL Foundation to a high school or youth football program in their name.

5th annual John Madden Thanksgiving Celebration takes place NEXT week across the @NFL!

Each of the 3 Thanksgiving Day games will feature the following:

🏈Commemorative coin w/ a silhouette of Coach Madden on one side & a Turducken on the reverse

🏈Jersey patch of Coach Madden… pic.twitter.com/0HeUO5JLIx

— NFL Media (@NFLMedia) November 20, 2026

Madden, one of the defining figures of the sport as both a coach and broadcaster, died in 2021 at the age of 85. Alongside longtime broadcasting partner Pat Summerall, Madden called NFL games for decades on CBS and later Fox, becoming associated with Thanksgiving games thanks to his enthusiasm for turduckens and turkey legs.

The league first introduced the specialized Madden patches and coins in 2023, two years after the football legend's death, and have continued the tradition over the past few years.

item.description: You should be able to see this one
item.content:encoded:
This Sunday’s game at U.S. Bank Stadium between the Atlanta Falcons and the Minnesota Vikings will feature Kirk Cousins’ return to the Twin Cities as the Vikings’ quarterback to take on the team he left Minnesota for before the 2024 season. It’s one of the more interesting storylines of Week 12 of this NFL season, and a pretty significant chunk of the country will be able to see it on over-the-air television.

The folks from 506 Sports have released their broadcast maps for this Week 12, and the FOX map for this week is below. The Falcons/Vikings game is represented by the red area.

As you can see, the portion of the country that will get Falcons/Vikings is pretty large, encompassing most of the western and northern United States, as well as a decent portion of the south. This will also be the game being shown to viewers in Alaska and Hawai’i. The other two games in the early window on FOX are the New York Giants at the Indianapolis Colts (represented by the blue area) and the Tennessee Titans at the Jacksonville Jaguars (represented by the green area).

Because of all the other games that have been interspersed throughout this Thanksgiving week, there will only be six games in the Sunday early window between FOX and CBS (and only three in the late window, so pray for Scott Hanson’s sanity, Red Zone viewers). That could also play a role in why the viewing area for Falcons/Vikings is as wide as it is.

There’s your broadcast coverage map for Week 12, folks. Hopefully there are quite a few of you who are in the red area on the map for this week’s game.

item.title: Steelers owner breaks silence on ‘insubordinate’ Aaron Rodgers — and reveals Mike McCarthy’s fate
item.description: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy has the support of team owner Art Rooney after Aaron Rodgers accused his now former coach of sleeping on the job.
item.content:encoded:
Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy has the support of team president and owner Art Rooney after Aaron Rodgers accused his now former coach of sleeping on the job.

Rooney made it clear that McCarthy’s job is safe in a statement to the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette on Thursday — and he called out Rodgers for “insubordination” regarding the quarterback blasting McCarthy on-air during Wednesday’s installment of “The Pat McAfee Show.”

“I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney said. “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.”

Rooney added that Rodgers was not a “good teammate” when explaining why the Steelers released him.

McCarthy said he benched Rodgers after the former four-time NFL MVP presented an “ultimatum” that was “clearly outside of his job description.”

McCarthy didn’t elaborate on their “private conversations.”

The Steelers announced Tuesday night that Rodgers would be inactive against Denver this week, and that Mason Rudolph would replace him.

After that, Rodgers did a surprise TV appearance Wednesday and accused McCarthy of sleeping during team meetings.

He also said McCarthy missed a walk-through Friday and a meeting Saturday morning before the Steelers’ 19-16 loss to the Eagles on Sunday — adding that it’s allegedly a known behavioral pattern exhibited by McCarthy in the Steelers’ building.

Rodgers was released Wednesday shortly after the interview.

item.title: Steelers owner Art Rooney II says Aaron Rodgers was not a 'good teammate,' expresses confidence in Mike McCarthy
item.description: Art Rooney II is happy with the way the Steelers responded Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are feeling good about their decision-making following the fallout from Aaron Rodgers' appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday. Rodgers was promptly released from the team and head coach Mike McCarthy was retained despite some scandalous accusations from his former quarterback.

While it was overall a pretty awful day for the team, Steelers owner Art Rooney II expressed optimism Thursday, saying he has "100 percent confidence in Mike McCarthy," via an interview with the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette.

Rooney also spoke about the decision to release Rodgers, saying the quarterback was not being a "good teammate" when he publicly aired the team's grievances following his benching, per the Post-Gazette.

"There's maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload," Rooney said. "He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure."

Then he added, "In general, I think, historically, what's in the locker room stays in the locker room. That's the way it's always been. That's the way it should be as far as I'm concerned."

Rodgers didn't take that track. Instead, the quarterback ripped his head coach relentlessly during an appearance on McAfee's show. Rodgers claimed McCarthy routinely fell asleep during meetings, led the team in a "1-2-3 Packers" chant and questioned the coach's physical health.

Rooney addressed that final accusation, saying McCarthy is "as healthy as the rest of us." The owner added, "health is not an issue."

Rooney then further continued to express support for McCarthy, saying the coach took criticism for changes Rodgers made during games, particularly in the red zone.

"The sad thing is Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called, particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had," Rooney said. "Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. He tried to protect him, and it just wasn't working."

Rooney then confirmed that Rodgers was released after trying to deliver an ultimatum to McCarthy. Rodgers reportedly said he wanted to call offensive plays or be released. McCarthy told Rodgers he doesn't get to make those calls, and decided to bench the veteran with the intention of releasing him in the coming days. Rodgers apparently fast-tracked that release with his interview on Wednesday.

The owner also expressed confidence in now-starter Mason Rudolph, saying the team was "excited and lucky" to have him step into the starting role.

At 6-4, the Steelers are still very much in the playoff hunt in the AFC. And after everything that occurred Wednesday, it might take a playoff appearance to salvage McCarthy's tenure with the franchise.

Rooney may have given the coach a vote of confidence, but Rodgers' words will be tough to ignore if the team continues to struggle on the field.

item.title: Rams PFF grades: Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett turn back clock
item.description: Big nights from Aaron Donald, Myles Garrett result in three turnovers by Packers offense
item.content:encoded:
The first NFL pre-Thanksgiving game brought a delicious victory for the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night. LA defeated the Green Bay Packers 26-13 to move to 7-4 on the season. After starting 2-4, winning five-straight didn’t seem to be in the cards. Their fortune seems to be shifting even in the face of injury.

Who stood out on an individual level from this game? Let’s review the Pro Football Focus (PFF) grades and data in order to lean into some analytical takeaways.

*Final grades are not currently available as of the writing of this post. Due to the Thanksgiving holiday I am going to run with the data still under review. Close enough.

Top five grades on offense

1 – Konata Mumpfield, WR: 77.0

Mumpfield was the Rams’ passing offense on Wednesday night. He earned 69 yards on four catches and provided the only threat vertically. The next closest pass catchers in terms of yardage were Blake Corum at 21 and Kyren Williams at 19. Xavier Smith was the only other receiver to catch a pass and his solo reception went for four yards.

Is that a reliable way to play offense and win games? Not really. The Rams must find better answers from their receiver group. They cannot rely on Davante Adams to completely reverse their fortunes on his own, especially coming back from a significant injury this late into his career.

2 – Justin Dedich, LG: 76.2

Dedich filled in for the injured Bill Murray who had replaced Steve Avila in the starting lineup. Dedich always seems to fare well in terms of PFF grading, and it’s encouraging to see him pickup where he left off after suffering an injury this summer that has limited his availability. Dedich is undersized. That may prevent him from ever becoming a full-time starter. He still has value in a reserve role.

3 – Tyler Higbee, TE: 75.2

Veteran tight end Tyler Higbee’s most important contributions came as a run blocker where he earned a mark from PFF of 70.2. He added one catch for 14 yards and came close to another big play. Higbee played roughly half the game before suffering an injury and being ruled out. Davis Allen was also ruled out. The statuses of both are worth monitoring moving forward.

4 – Blake Corum, RB: 71.6

What more is there to say about Blake Corum’s performance not just Wednesday night but over the last seven weeks? Against the Packers he grinded out 184 yards and a score for an average of 5.80. PFF credited the back with 103 yards after contact (3.22 average). The offensive line was road grading as well, as they generated 2.58 yards before contact on Corum’s carries. Not a bad day at the office.

5 – Beaux Limmer, C: 70.9

It would be a welcome development—given the amount of players across the Rams’ roster that need new contracts—if Limmer could takeover the starting center job on a going forward basis. Injured starter Coleman Shelton is approaching the end of his 2025 free agent deal. Limmer has one year left on his rookie contract. He continues to excel in pass protection in the middle of the offensive line.

Other notes on offense

Matthew Stafford finished 17th in grades out of the 19 players who appeared on offense. PFF graded him at a mark of 54.2. The outlet did not credit the veteran quarterback with a single big-time throw. He had one turnover-worthy play that resulted into an interception that could have proved costly; however, Jordan Love made a mistake of his own just two plays later.

Stafford has now thrown an interception in all but two of 11 games this season. He’s at 11 on the year, so averaging one per game in the aggregate. If the Rams are going to be limited offensively and lean into ball control into order to constrict the opposition into submission, one requirement of that is taking care of the football. Can the Rams trust Stafford in this area? His track record so far this year suggests not.

Rams fans are waiting for Stafford to turn his season around. It hasn’t happened yet. He’s still the 21st-graded quarterback by both offensive grade and passing grade. It’s clear he has taken a major step back this year. The end could be nearer than expected.

It’s difficult to say anything other than 2027 seems to be Ty Simpson’s year to takeover.

Top five grades on defense

1 – Aaron Donald, DT: 93.5

Donald and Garrett each had five total pressures on Jordan Love even though neither finished with a sack. The Rams only brought down Love once (Bryon Young), although the pressure did ultimately force three turnovers by the Pakcers’ offense. Love easily could have finished with at least five interceptions—including dropped picks by Quentin Lake and Trent McDuffie and a takeaway by Kam Curl that was reversed because of penalty.

2 – Kamren Kinchens, DB: 90.5

Kinchens forced a major collision along the sideline with receiver Christian Watson that dramatically altered the rest of the game. Kinchens was ejected, which resulted in controversy. Watson entered concussion protocol and was ruled out for the second half. The Rams seemingly had no answers for the dynamic receiver up to that point, and the Packers had little going through the air in the second half without Watson.

3 – Myles Garrett, EDGE: 90.2

4 – Nate Landman, MLB: 89.9

Make it another hallmark punch out for Nate Landman. He stole the ball away from tight end Tucker Kraft for a key takeaway.

The veteran linebacker played just 25 snaps. Omar Speights had 10. Shaun Dolac played seven. The roles of these players are changing as Lake took over the green dot duties. That isn’t necessarily a bad thing. The defensive line is limiting opposing rushing attacks on their own. The Rams are able to pivot more towards additional safeties to focus on tightening up through the air. It’s working. Stick with it.

5 – Quentin Lake, DB: 89.4

Lake finished with the second-highest coverage grade on the defense (87.0) behind only Landman (90.5). He dropped an interception that likely would have scored and put the Packers away even earlier. In total he finished with two pass breakups.

Other notes on defense

The Packers went after reserve corners Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes often with mixed results. Each had four targets into their coverage. Wallace allowed three receptions for 15 yards and the touchdown to Watson. Forbes gave up three catches for 79 yards (36 after the catch) and he caught the interception that effectively sealed the game.

While their PFF marks were low relative to the other members of the defense (18th and 19th out of 20), these coverage numbers aren’t something that will get you beat. The standard is not perfection for these players as they look to replace injured starter Jaylen Watson. There will be negative moments. The Rams must hope that the positives—like Forbes’ interception—outweigh the bad.

item.title: Chiefs-Bills: 5 questions with Buffalo Rumblings ahead of Week 12
item.description: We welcome Buffalo Rumblings for answers to five questions about Buffalo before Thursday Night’s Week 12 matchup.
item.content:encoded:
Tonight, the Kansas City Chiefs face the Buffalo Bills in a week 12 Thanksgiving’s night showdown. We welcome Matthew Byham of Buffalo Rumblings— our sister SBNation site covering the Bills— for Five Questions with the Enemy.

Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app!

Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time.

  • Chat live throughout the game
  • Browse with fewer ads
  • Easily jump between communities
  • Enjoy faster commenting and posting

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android.

Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device and join the Buffalo Rumblings community through Sunday’s game to get perspectives from both sides of the Week 12 matchup!

1. Buffalo converted only two of its five red-zone possessions into touchdowns against Miami and now faces the NFL’s top-ranked red-zone defense. What must the Bills improve inside the 20-yard line to finish drives against Kansas City?

It wasn’t all that surprising to me that Josh Allen and the Bills struggled to convert red zone trips into touchdowns. The Miami Dolphins under Jeff Hafley field a top-10 defense and they put together a great game plan. Unfortunately, their surprising talent is overshadowed by the mess on offense. Divisional matchups are always unpredictable, no matter any lack of familiarity (i.e., Dolphins having new coaching/roster overhaul).

The team would never admit it, but I also have to wonder if Buffalo was holding some things back a bit with a very important game only a few days later. Not necessarily in an effort to hide plays (because at this point there’s a lot of tape on every team), but rather pacing themselves for the marathon ahead.

Not to take anything away from a Dolphins team that seems to be on the right track, but the Bills never trailed in that game. Head coach Joe Brady probably felt that even accumulating field goals might be too much for Miami’s offense to counter.

As to your question about what the Bills need to improve? First and foremost, it would be great if tight end Dalton Kincaid (questionable w/thumb, ankle) were able to play in this one. He missed last week, and it’s pretty evident that Brady’s offense is vastly superior with Kincaid involved — especially as a red zone target.

But drilling down further, the Bills struggle to gain separation on routes, and it’s magnified in the red zone.

Buffalo would also do well to leverage their running game more near the goal line in this one. Sometimes I believe Brady gets a bit cute trying to outsmart a defense when, time and again, they’ve proven almost impossible to stop in the trenches this season.

I’d like to see Brady roll out with two running backs near the goal line. It’s rare for him to do that anywhere on the field, even though Ty Johnson is the team’s most reliable pass catcher. Pairing Johnson with James Cook III in goal-to-go situations, while accounting for Allen’s dual threat, could create real havoc for a defense. Brady just has to be willing to shift out of a few 13-personnel plays, while finding the shortest path from point A to B.

2.  Josh Allen did not record a rushing attempt against Miami, marking the first full game of his career without one. How aggressively should Buffalo use Allen’s legs against a Chiefs defense that has historically struggled to contain his extended plays?

Allen should run as instinct instructs, nothing more, nothing less. I wouldn’t expect Brady to confine him to one thing or another, aside from asking him to avoid arm punts in a game like this, and with weather that’s going to be suspect at best. Allowing Allen to play free from constraint is the best move, while giving him options to abort anything risky.

It is interesting that Allen didn’t rush a single time versus the Dolphins, but I’m left wondering if that was to protect him from any potential injury. Early on, Buffalo’s offense faced 4th & 1, and they ran a traditional handoff to Cook, who went right. It was a complete paradigm shift from what we’ve known of the Bills’ short-yardage offense. I expect him to have at least a few carries in this game, both in short- and long-yardage situations.

3. James Cook has surpassed 1,000 rushing yards and has recorded at least 75 rushing yards and a touchdown in nine consecutive games. How important will establishing Cook be in the expected cold and rainy conditions Thursday night?

James Cook is vital to the Bills’ success on offense. You could place bets on Buffalo leveraging Cook early and often, even if the weather was trending pleasant. Buffalo is 14-2 when Cook carries 20 times or more in a game. Under Brady, the Bills now employ a smash-mouth brand of football where they’ll remain committed to the run game even if it’s only getting a few yards a clip in early action.

Outsiders have begun to catch on that Brady’s system is heavy on the run, despite having Allen at quarterback. Somehow, Cook seems to be fairly overlooked in many circles despite leading the league in rushing last season and roughly 30 yards out of first place this season.

Cook is slight by typical NFL standards, but he’s proven tough between the tackles and moves like a hummingbird in traffic. With Cook and the maulers along the offensive line, Buffalo has been able to wear out defenses in a four-quarter battle of attrition.

4. Buffalo has not allowed a touchdown in three consecutive games and could regain several injured defenders against Kansas City. Is the Bills’ recent defensive improvement sustainable against a Chiefs offense that has scored at least 34 points in three straight games?

That’s the question everyone wants answered right now. It’s fair to say that Buffalo hasn’t faced the NFL’s best quarterbacks in the last four games, but there’s reason to be optimistic about their trajectory. That’s due to confidence, which is so important in this sport.

Early in the season, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard’s group was often out of position and visibly confused pre-snap. The pass rush was the only thing working, and mostly because Greg Rousseau has been a revelation as a 3-4 outside linebacker.

The secondary has played well of late, especially since moving on from safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson (first to Damar Hamlin and now Amani Hooker — the latter via trade). Cornerback Christian Benford has been elite, working to almost completely shut down tight end Brock Bowers and wide receiver Justin Jefferson, and holding wide receiver Zay Flowers to zero burger on the stat sheet.

Make no mistake, this is a huge challenge. Kelce will always be Kelce, right (he’s always so open!)? It seems like this may be the most productive group of pass catchers KC’s had since Tyreek Hill wore red. Will they hold the Chiefs under their 34-point average in the last three games? It’s impossible to know, but at the same time the Bills are a different caliber of team compared to the New York Jets, Atlanta Falcons (what an epic defensive drop this season), and Arizona Cardinals.

It’s similar to Buffalo, where the Chiefs are either more complete or far better than the Baltimore Ravens, Minnesota Vikings, Jets, or Dolphins. I think we find out a lot more about both teams Thanksgiving night.

5.Buffalo has won five consecutive regular-season meetings against Kansas City, and the winner will take control of the AFC’s No. 1 seed. What is your prediction for how this Thanksgiving night matchup unfolds, including the final score?

I know that many Chiefs fans like to say that the regular-season matchup means little, and that Buffalo has yet to defeat Mahomes and company in the postseason. However, this is a massive game simply because of the playoff bye that’s at stake.

Allen and the Bills have never earned the one seed, which I believe harmed prior rosters as it relates to injury recovery/availability in the playoffs under McDermott. Currently in control of the one seed, I’d venture to guess that Allen and company are going to be locked-in and ready to take a more firm hold on the lead.

I understand you’re hoping for a final score prediction, but I never pick Bills games. I think they have as good a chance as any team to defeat KC, given their season-long consistency as a dominant throwback offense. Even if the defense gives up 34 points, Allen and Cook are fully capable of besting it with 35 or more.

If it’s a low-scoring affair instead due to weather, I expect Buffalo and Kansas City to each try bleeding the clock through the run game. That might be both teams’ plan A regardless of the situation. The Bills are built to both bully the clock and go toe-to-toe in a shootout.

Sounds a bit like the Chiefs, right?

Who wins? I’d say since both teams are once again playoff favorites, they each have a pretty fair shot at postgame turkey. It comes down to the red zone, and maybe a two-point conversion or two. We’ll find out what’s what soon enough in what should be a thrilling Turkey Day nightcap!

item.title: Buffalo Bills OLB Greg Rousseau single-handedly wrecking NFL offenses
item.description: Buffalo Bills OLB Greg Rousseau is a 1-man wrecking machine who’s having a career season, while those around him have failed to produce much as pass rushers
item.content:encoded:
To say that Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau is having a career year in 2026 is quite the understatement. Rousseau leads the NFL in quarterback hits with 29, and is currently second league-wide with 10 sacks in 10 games this season. His current sack total is a new career high for Rousseau — the first time in his professional career he’s reach double-digits in that category.

Rousseau deserves to be mentioned in NFL Defensive Player of the Year conversations. He seems to be a good candidate as an All-Pro selection, and is likely to receive Pro Bowl honors.

His success comes following a switch this offseason to 3-4 outside linebacker after playing the previous five seasons as a defensive end in a 4-3 system. It’s the first time in Rousseau’s career that he’s played that role as an edge rusher out wide from the linebacker box.

When you run through Rousseau’s stats this year, it’s easy to imagine that he’s thrilled with the position shift. In just over half a season to this point, Rousseau has set new career highs in sacks (10), quarterback hits (29), and pass defenses (8); while tying his career high in forced fumbles (3), and remains just four off his single-season-career-best of 16 tackles for loss.

When new Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady hired Jim Leonhard as the team’s current defensive coordinator, many were very curious how the former Bills safety intended to implement the attack-based system he espoused. After all, Leonhard had never called a team’s defensive plays at the NFL level, and he decided to make sweeping changes while marching forward with a large group of players hand-picked by prior head coach Sean McDermott.

With the benefit of hindsight, it’s now clear that Rousseau may have been miscast as a do-it-all defensive end left to battle it out in the trenches. He played well there for McDermott, of course, but the brand of game-wrecking energy now regularly seen was at best available in spurts with him so deeply tied up in close hand combat against offensive linemen.

Leonhard and outside linebackers coach Bobby April III have transformed Rousseau into the sort of player who keeps other teams’ offensive coordinators up and worrying about game plans. In his new role, Rousseau uses his albatross-like wingspan and skyscraper height to out-leverage would-be blockers. His reach and hands have become a problem for most quarterbacks, sometimes to the detriment of their depth chart.

Rousseau’s jump in production is staggering, quite honestly, just from a quick glance at his career numbers via Pro Football Reference:

In preparing to face the Bills on Thanksgiving, Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy was quick to praise the man he nicknamed “Stretch Armstrong,” adding that KC’s defense must do what it can “neutralize his strengths” and “have a plan in place, making sure that we’re putting bodies on him and keeping him off our quarterback.”

It’s been quite some time since Buffalo had an edge rusher who instilled such fear among NFL teams, maybe dating back to defensive end Mario Williams. Now, Leonhard and the Bills must find a way to get better production out of the team’s other front-seven defenders.

Amid all the praise for Rousseau’s game in 2026 comes a worrying trend when evaluating his defensive teammates. Though Rousseau is a 1-man wrecking machine who’s having a career season, teammates around him have failed to produce much as pass rushers.

After Rousseau, there’s a steep drop in production and impact plays among the defensive line and outside linebackers. Defensive linemen Ed Oliver and Deone Walker have received praise in year one within Leonhard’s system, but the overall sack production beyond Rousseau has been dreadful.

Defensive lineman T.J. Parker ranks second on the team with 3.5 sacks. Nine other players on the team have chipped in toward the sack total, however those nine defenders have only 9.5 sacks combined. Quick math reveals that Rousseau has more sacks than all Bills defenders, not named Parker, added together.

Buffalo’s schedule over the next month is a gauntlet, and the defense will be tested beyond the trials early this season. Someone must step up in a complementary role as a pass rusher in tandem with Rousseau, otherwise teams may begin implementing new ways of slowing down the Bills’ best defender.

In the four games since Buffalo’s bye week, the defense has played a far more aggressive brand of football. Perhaps Leonhard’s only just begun scratching the surface of the pressure package he intends to release on the NFL. A big test awaits Thursday night.

item.title: Art Rooney II expresses support for Mike McCarthy, calls Aaron Rodgers not a "good teammate"
item.description: Steelers owner speaks about Wednesday's insanity.
item.content:encoded:
After Wednesday's unprecedented chaos, it had to happen. And it did.

Steelers owner Art Rooney II has addressed the events that resulted in the benching and then the firing of quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

“A change had to be made, and I certainly agree with the change and the way it was handled," Rooney told Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette in a Thursday interview.

The change was sparked by the notion that Rodgers gave coach Mike McCarthy an ultimatum: “Either let me call all the plays or just release me.” Instead, McCarthy benched him.

It went to the next level when, as many expected, Rodgers scurried to the McAfee show to take shots at McCarthy for missing meetings, showing up late to meetings, and falling asleep in meetings — among other things, including the ultra-embarrassing "1-2-3 Packers!" moment from halftime of Sunday's loss to the Eagles.

“There’s maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload,” Rooney said. “He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that’s for sure. . . .

“In general, I think, historically, what’s in the locker room stays in the locker room. That’s the way it’s always been. That’s the way it should be as far as I’m concerned.”

Rooney also confirmed that the team supports McCarthy, despite Rodgers's rant and reports confirming the facts underpinning the petty delivery of them.

“I just want to say that I have 100 [percent] confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney told Dulac. “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.”

Rooney also was asked whether Rodgers raised with the owner supposed concerns about McCarthy's health.

“Nothing,” Rooney said. “Mike’s as healthy as the rest of us. Health was not an issue. I’m not sure where that part comes [from].”

Rooney also addressed something that has been largely overlooked during the fast-moving drama: Rodgers's subpar performance.

“The sad thing is Mike took some of the bullets for Aaron in terms of some of the plays that were called, particularly in the red-zone troubles that we had,” Rooney said. “Mike took some of the bullets for things that were going wrong down there. He tried to protect him, and it just wasn’t working.”

They should have known it wouldn't work between Rodgers and McCarthy. It's still unclear why either one of them thought it would. McCarthy shouldn't have wanted a reunion with Rodgers. And Rodgers shouldn't have wanted a second act with McCarthy.

Then again, it's not as if Rodgers had many choices. In 2025, he had few takers. In 2026, he had fewer. If he was going to ensure that his final NFL throw wasn't a pick-six by playing another year, Pittsburgh wasn't just the best place.

It was likely the only place.

item.title: Detroit Lions vs. Chicago Bears: Live score updates, highlights, injury news
item.description: Live score updates and highlights from Detroit Lions vs. Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving.
item.content:encoded:
It’s a huge NFC North showdown to kick off the NFL’s Thanksgiving tripleheader on Thursday.

The Detroit Lions are 8-2 and trying to win their third division title in four years. They’ve endured a fair share of injuries as of late, particularly on defense. Captains Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson are on injured reserve, while Detroit will also be missing defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard, defensive end DJ Wonnum, and safety Chuck Clark in this matchup.

However, despite all of that, the Lions are winners of six straight. Their offense is hitting its stride, with the offensive line gelling and the run game explosive. Plus, Jared Goff is in the middle of yet another dominant year.

But the Chicago Bears will be one of the toughest tests the Lions will see all season. They’re also 8-2 on the season and on a five-game winning streak of their own. The addition of Jeffery Simmons on defense has turned a good defense into a great one. And while there have been struggles in the run game, quarterback Caleb Williams has taken his game to another level.

Who walks away with the W in this big NFC North game? Stay tuned right here to find out.

This article will populate with updates from Ford Field, including drive-by-drive analysis, score updates, game highlights, and injury news. All you need to do is stay on this site, and hit refresh when the game kicks off and watch as the updates and news come in. By the end of the game, this will be our game recap post.

Enjoy your Thanksgiving and go Lions!

First quarter

The Lions won the toss and elected to take the ball first, in a change of normal strategy. Detroit’s offense got off to a strong start with a 6 and 7 yard run from Jahmyr Gibbs and a 19-yard pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown.

Starting right guard Tate Ratledge exited the field with a limp and went straight to the blue tent. He was replaced by Miles Frazier. Ratledge was initially ruled questionable to return with an ankle and knee injury. He would return to the lineup after missing the next drive.

But the Lions kept driving, and St. Brown made a ridiculous one-handed, 27-yard catch to put the Lions first-and-goal from the 9-yard line.

However, the Lions stalled from there with back-to-back incomplete passes from Goff, and Detroit had to settle for a chip-shot field goal. 3-0 Lions.

The Bears quickly drove down the field, with Caleb Williams finding a few wide-open receivers, including D’Andre Swift for 13 yards and Kalif Raymond for 12. But when they moved into the red zone, Lions rookie defensive end Derrick Moore punched the ball out of Coleston Loveland’s hands and Malcolm Rodriguez recovered the fumble for a big turnover.

Detroit took over at their own 16, but quickly went three-and-out. A pitch to Gibbs was snuffed out by the Bears, turning a second-and-3 into a third-and-6. And Goff couldn’t find anyone open on third down, eventually throwing a ball off St. Brown’s fingertips for an incomplete pass.

But Detroit’s defense answered the call with a forced three-and-out of their own. A nice pressure from Anthony Lucas nearly forced an interception on second down, and Luther Burden was tackled well short of the sticks on third down by safety Andre Cisco, who was in for Chuck Clark.

On the drive, Bears tight end Colston Loveland was carted to the locker room.

Detroit’s passing attack hit another big play—a seam route to St. Brown for 23 yards. The All-Pro receiver took a big hit, but managed to hold onto the ball to put the Lions at their own 40-yard line.

A facemask penalty gave the Lions another 15 yards, and pushed them into Bears territory. Then a 14-yard catch from Gibbs and an 11-yard run by Jameson Williams moved the Lions into the red zone as the first quarter expired.

Second quarter

On a third-and-3 play, Gibbs ran up the gut for a 9-yard gain down to the Bears’ 1-yard line. Two plays later, Gibbs’ second effort pushed Detroit into the end zone for a 10-0 Lions lead early in the second quarter.

The Bears quickly answered with an explosive run. Salvon Ahmed broke off a 46-yard gain down the right sideline and into the red zone.

But Detroit locked them down from there. Derrick Moore picked up a sack on first down.

Then, on third-and-long, a blitzing Roger McCreary knocked down the pass at the line of scrimmage to hold the Bears to three. 10-3 Lions.

Detroit’s next drive was marred by back-to-back false starts from center Juice Scruggs. That forced a third-and-11, and Jared Goff, with all sorts of time, tried to check it down to Sione Vaki, but missed him.

item.title: Steelers President Art Rooney expresses full confidence in Mike McCarthy
item.description: Steelers President Art Rooney II backs Mike McCarthy amidst Aaron Rodgers saga.
item.content:encoded:
Wednesday was one of the wildest days in the history of the Pittsburgh Steelers. After benching Aaron Rodgers late Tuesday night, the four-time MVP went on The Pat McAfee Show and aired out a lot of grievances largely pertaining to head coach Mike McCarthy.

Among the issues Rodgers put on blast were McCarthy routinely falling asleep in meetings, being late for walkthroughs and meetings, not knowing the gameplay, and breaking down a team huddle vs. the Eagles by saying, “1-2-3 Packers.”

Several insiders have noted that players have backed up these claims made by Rodgers, which led many to believe McCarthy’s days in Pittsburgh could and should be numbered. However, Team President Art Rooney II expressed faith in the Steelers’ head coach.

“I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney said via Gerry Dulac. “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.”

The Steeles will face the Broncos on Black Friday in their first home game since they defeated the Cleveland Browns 27-6 to secure a 6-2 record. Oh how much has changed since then.

item.content:encoded:
Happy Thanksgiving, Ultimate Fans! What a weekend for football, complete with NFL drama and everything! A few short days ago we were salivating over the chance to sack Aaron Rodgers and then he went and sacked himself…making the Broncos’ game Friday more interesting to say the least. Or as our awesome UFGer noted, “more unpredictable!”

Another huge thanks to this week’s contributor, Wrenchman1122, who’s been pulling for this team for a loooonnnnngggg time, and he’s ready for another Super Bowl run. (and since it’s Thanksgiving, let me just say a huge thanks to ALL of you — the contributors and the commenters — who come here every week to give and react to such excellent insights and fun commentary. I say it every year and I mean every time — I LOVE THIS SERIES MORE THAN ANY OTHER POST I WRITE!)

But now let’s kick off this Thanksgiving football weekend with a bang! GO BRONCOS!

Week 12: Broncos at Steelers

MHR – Broncos are 8-2, coming off a win over the Raiders, sitting alone atop the AFC West and knocking on the door to the overall No. 1 seed in the AFC. How good is life for a Broncos fan right now?
Wrenchman1122: It’s been a heck of a ride so far, especially the one-score games. Life is pretty darn good in Broncos Country right now!  What I love most is that this team is winning in different ways. We have Nix who keeps growing, an offense with multiple weapons, and a defense that can make life miserable for anybody.  Beating the Raiders is always sweet and with first place in the West all to ourselves and looking to catch the Bills?  Even better!  

MHR – Big news on a short week – JK Dobbins suspended and Aaron Rodgers benched. While the Dobbins news may not impact the offense all that much, Rodgers’ decision has been…interesting. In general how do these two pieces of info impact the kind of game the Broncos should play on offense and defense? Likewise, with the short week and East Coast game, does this push Payton toward a simpler, run-heavy game plan?
Wrenchman1122:  I like our chances if we make them play our game.  A different theory, this week – pass early to set up the run as Pittsburgh has a good run D and the secondary can be taken advantage of, especially on quick hits with Waddle in motion or Sutton bodying up the defender. And let’s keep using Engram and his speed, which was evident last week against the dreaded Raiders.  

The weather will play havoc with specific planning, and with Rogers being benched and ultimately released, I’d expect plenty of runs and quick throws to help Rudolph get settled.  We need to stop the run…if we can stop the run, we have an excellent chance. The short week, East Coast game and weather may create a simpler game plan, but we have the advantage of a mid-season form Nix versus Rudolph who has only started a handful (19?) games. 

MHR – Jonah Coleman has seemed like “the guy” a few times this season and then he broke it open on Sunday. Granted, the Raiders have one of the worst run defenses in the league, but what are your thoughts on Hat Trick Coleman and making him the bell cow back? And have we seen the last of Dobbins in Denver?
Wrenchman1122:  I’m all in on Jonah Coleman. Sure, the Raiders weren’t exactly known for stopping the run, but you still have to go out there and do it. Three touchdowns, 111 yards rushing, and the way he ran with authority, vision, and determination tell me we’re watching something special develop. What impressed me most wasn’t just the numbers; it was how he took over when the game was on the line. That’s what you want to see from a running back.

I believe Coleman has earned the opportunity to be the bell cow. Feed the hot hand! He’s physical, runs with a purpose, and seems to get stronger as the game goes on. He’s also giving this offense something it desperately needs: a dependable running game that takes pressure off Bo Nix and opens up the passing attack. As for Dobbins, I wouldn’t write him off just yet. He’s been a good player for Denver, but this is a business, and opportunities have to be earned. With the recent suspension and Coleman’s emergence, the situation has certainly changed.

Here’s my bottom line – Broncos Country has been waiting for an offense that can run the ball, control the clock, and finish games physically. Coleman might be exactly the missing piece we’ve been looking for. Between Bo Nix, this defense, and a running game that’s starting to find its identity, I like what I’m seeing.  (Love the Hat-Trick reference). 

MHR – The Broncos really do have a lot of offensive targets to use, and Bo Nix alluded to that after the Raiders game in talking about Evan Engram’s big day, noting that he, like many others on the team, “probably want to get the ball more.” Of all the receiving threats – Sutton, Waddle, Bryant, Engram, Mims… – who do you think are the best for this offense and is it possible to have too much of a good thing and still keep all of it?
Wrenchman1122: I love this problem. When was the last time we could honestly say the Broncos had this many weapons on offense?  Jaylen Waddle brings something Denver hasn’t had enough of: game-changing speed. He forces defenses to respect the deep ball and opens things up underneath for everyone else.  I was impressed with Engram’s game last week.  We finally were able to be reminded of what he can do. He’s a matchup nightmare for linebackers and safeties, and I want to see him become a bigger part of the weekly game plan.  Defenses can’t take away everybody. Double Sutton, and Waddle can burn you. Take away the deep ball, and Engram can work the middle. Crowd the middle, and Bryant or Mims can make you pay. Add Jonah Coleman establishing a legitimate running game, and suddenly this offense becomes awfully difficult to defend.

MHR – I thought the Raiders game was one of Nix’s best, even if the stat line wasn’t particularly impressive. What did you like, what should Nix and the offense build on, and what still needs work – particularly as we gear up for what could be a major showdown for the AFC with the Bills in a month?
Wrenchman1122:  I thought Bo showed real growth against the Raiders. What I liked most was his patience, decision-making, and willingness to take what the defense gave him rather than forcing plays. The connection with his receivers is continuing to develop, and the running game is finally giving this offense another dimension. That’s what we need to build on. What still needs work is consistency, especially on third downs, red-zone execution, and avoiding unnecessary turnovers. Against a team like Buffalo, you can’t afford to leave points on the field. I believe Bo is growing into the quarterback we hoped he would be, and I wouldn’t trade our guy for anybody. 

MHR – Matt Peart, not Alex Palczewski or Ben Powers, started the game at left guard, and Bo Nix got sacked just once. Payton indicated that “Powers is still important to what we’re doing” but is Peart the answer at left guard? Or was that a one-week patch?
Wrenchman1122: I think Peart earned another look at left guard. The line played well against the Raiders, and keeping Bo upright has to be priority No.1. One game doesn’t make Peart the permanent answer, but I’d like to see what he can do with another opportunity. Powers remains an important piece. Not sure he’s 100% and Palczewski provides valuable depth. Ultimately, let the best five linemen earn their spots. 

MHR – Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback while Rodgers will be inactive on another team! It’ll be Rudolph’s 20th career start. Does the QB change make Pittsburgh more dangerous or less? How should Vance Joseph attack a QB who just got the keys midweek? Wrenchman1122:  I think the quarterback change makes Pittsburgh a little more unpredictable, but I wouldn’t necessarily say more dangerous. Rudolph has experience and has shown he can win games, so Vance Joseph can’t afford to take him lightly. The key is to make him uncomfortable early. Bring pressure, disguise coverages, mix up the looks, and force him to make quick decisions. At the same time, Denver has to stay disciplined and not give up easy plays by getting too aggressive. I want to see our defense set the tone, create a turnover, and make Rudolph prove he can beat us. If the Broncos control the line of scrimmage and get after him, I like our chances.

MHR – Ja’Quan McMillian. This guy is unbelievable. On a defense with a future HOF cornerback and All Pro edge rushers and d-linemen, J-Mac just goes and does it all anyway. What impresses you about him and is he just getting more expensive by the game for George Paton? 😉
Wrenchman1122:  McMillian is everything you want in a Broncos defender. His instincts, toughness, versatility, and ability to make plays in big moments are impressive. What I love most is that he plays with a chip on his shoulder and never seems intimidated by the moment. Honestly, J-Mac reminds me a little of Rod Smith. Maybe it’s the underdog mentality, the work ethic, or the way he constantly proves people wrong. He may not get the headlines that Surtain and the pass rushers get, but he’s a huge part of what makes this defense special. George Paton has an important decision ahead of him because McMillian is making a strong case for a well-deserved payday. He’s a player I’d like to see wearing orange and blue for a long, long time.

MHR – While the Broncos’ defense has turned in amazing plays to win a lot of games this season, there are still some holes…especially defending the run and the middle of the field. Are you concerned? Is this a personnel problem or just an issue of giving up a few big plays here and there?
Wrenchman1122:  As good as this defense has been, I think there are areas that still need improvement. The biggest thing this defense needs to clean up is eliminating the two or three explosive plays it seems to give up each game. Championship defenses don’t just make big plays; they limit the opponent’s opportunities to make them. Singleton has played extremely well in the middle, but his pass coverage can still be an issue at times. My biggest concern, however, is depth. Injuries are inevitable, and we need to know the next man up can maintain the same level of play. I don’t think it’s time to panic, but these are areas that need attention. Come playoff time, teams will expose any weakness they can find, and we need all three levels of this defense playing at a high level.

MHR – Special teams last week turned in two blocked punts. And Crawshaw and Lutz have been spectacular. Is Special Teams a true strength for the Broncos that can be the difference-maker in closer games and/or playoffs down the stretch?
Wrenchman1122:  Absolutely. Special teams can be a major difference-maker, especially in tight games and the playoffs. Two blocked punts show the aggressiveness and preparation of this unit, while Crawshaw and Lutz have been outstanding. Just as importantly, it forces opposing teams to spend valuable practice time preparing for what Denver can do on special teams rather than focusing entirely on our offense and defense. I consider special teams a real strength for Denver and potentially a deciding factor down the stretch.

MHR – Not to get too far ahead, but what is your hope for this team this season?
Wrenchman1122:  My hope is to see Denver make a legitimate run at the Super Bowl. I think this team has the talent, coaching, and defensive identity to compete with anybody. The biggest thing is consistency, staying healthy, and continuing to develop on offense. I want to see the defense remain aggressive, the offense take another step forward, and this team learn how to win the close games against the best competition. At a minimum, I want a playoff run that gives Broncos Country something to be excited about.  The optimist in me wants the 49ers again in Super Bowl LXI.  

Predictions  

Stats for Bo Nix?  18-37 205 yards, 1 TD, 0 interceptions 

Stats for Jonah Coleman and any other RB?  22/66, 1 score.  Badie/Schrader 4-10, 0 TDs

Number of yards/TDs for Waddle, Sutton, Bryant, Franklin?  (Waddle 5-66) (Sutton 4-51) (Bryant 2-19) Franklin (1-8)  

Number of yards/TDs for Trautman, Engram? (Trautman 1-5) (Engram 5-56)

Longest FG for Lutz?  48 yards

Number of sacks to Aaro…Mason Rudolph?  3

Broncos player with the most tackles?   Singleton 

Who gets the first sack of the game for the Broncos?  Allen, he’s been on a “heater” 

How many INTs/FF/FR for the Steelers’ D?   0 

How many INTs/FF/FR for the Broncos’ D?  1 

Final Score?  19-14 Broncos 

The Favorites 

Favorite John Elway win outside of the Super Bowls? Wow, loaded question waaay to many… I’ll go back to his early years when the “Boz” was the new toy in the league and came to Denver and was schooled  by Elway 40-17 (09/13/1987).  The first game my wife and I attended.  

Favorite Peyton Manning win? The comeback that started it all.  Down 24-0 to the Chargers in San Diego (10/15/2012) and came back to win.  Started a great 4 years of being a fan!    

Favorite win by any other QB? Jake Plummer when he beat Tom Brady @ Mile High, 27-13 (Jan. 14, 2006)  

Favorite Broncos win ever? No question, the first Superbowl win XXXII 

Team you love to beat the most in the AFC West?  Chiefs.  I’m originally from Kansas and absolutely cannot stand the Chiefs.  Been a life-long Broncos fan since my dad took me to a game against the “Boston Patriots.” Yea, I’ve been around for a bit.       

Coach you laugh at the most in the NFL?  Jim Harbaugh.  More drama than a soap opera. 

Coach you most want to throat-punch?  Josh McDaniels. I’d do it twice.  

The team you hate to lose to the most in the rest of the AFC?   Chiefs-1A, Raiders-1B.  I’m old school, can’t stand the AFC West opponents and always want them to lose.  Chargers just Charger… 

NFC team you could cheer for in the Super Bowl?  49ers, because of Shanahan (and ONLY if the Broncos aren’t playing)  

NFC team you want to face more than any other in the Super Bowl?  49ers-revenge game. 

Favorite game so far this season?  The come-from-behind against KC. No question.

Favorite Broncos player on the current roster?  I’m a big Surtain fan…smooth and loves the game.  

Favorite Broncos player of all time not named John Elway (unless it is John Elway!)?  Tough question-always been an Elway fan due to his baseball days in New York.  Second in line would be the epitome of Denver – Champ Bailey.   

Favorite new guy/rookie on the team?  Love J’MAc and his feistiness.  Also, Coleman; he’s going to be special.   

Food/Snack you have to eat on game day? Any type of nut and chips.  

Favorite game analyst/commentator?  Old school – Madden; current – Jim Nance 

Who is on your Broncos’ Mount Rushmore?  Elway, Champ, Von and Floyd Little (Little put the city of Denver on the map; no longer a cow town!)

How did you become a Broncos fan?  

I grew up in Kansas, where most people naturally gravitated toward the Chiefs. My dad, however, was a Broncos fan, and I followed his lead. What started as cheering for the same team grew into a lifelong passion for Broncos football. Growing up in Chiefs country made it even more meaningful, especially during the rivalry years. Some of my earliest football memories were shaped by watching the Broncos, and that connection has stayed with me throughout the years. Today, my loyalty to Denver is as strong as ever, and being a Broncos fan is a tradition I’m proud to call my own.  Go Broncos!!

item.title: Brandon Aiyuk signs with Washington Commanders practice squad as free agent, reuniting with former college quarterback Jayden Daniels
item.description: Aiyuk is looking to play in his first NFL game since 2024.
item.content:encoded:
Veteran wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has officially signed with the Washington Commanders practice squad as a free agent, the team announced Thursday. Receiver Malik Heath was released from the practice squad in conjunction with the move.

We have made the following roster moves:
- Signed WR Brandon Aiyuk and CB Ambry Thomas to the practice squad
- Released WR Malik Heath from the practice squad

— Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 26, 2026

Aiyuk was released by the 49ers on Monday and passed through waivers on Tuesday, going unclaimed. Now, he reunites with his former teammate at Arizona State, quarterback Jayden Daniels.

The Commanders, fresh off a stunning upset over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 11, have been in need of help at receiver following a season-ending injury to star wideout Terry McLaurin. The team sits at 4-5-1, just two games back from the New York Giants, who hold the lead in the NFC East.

This marks a fresh start for the 28-year-old, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract extension with the 49ers ahead of the 2024 season but played just seven games on the new deal. He tore his ACL and MCL on Oct. 20, 2024, ending his season.

Aiyuk also missed the entirety of the 2025 season, with conflicting reports about his health as he rehabbed the knee injury. The distance between the two sides only grew as San Francisco voided his contract guarantees ahead of the 2025 season. Eventually, he was placed on the Reserve/Left Squad list in December 2025 due to his continued absence and lack of communication with the team.

This past January, 49ers GM John Lynch officially acknowledged the impending split, saying at his end-of-season news conference, "I think it's safe to say he's played his last snap with the 49ers."

Aiyuk was officially reinstated from the Reserve/Left Squad list on Nov. 9, at which time the 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption to decide if they wanted to release him, trade him or add him to the 53-man roster. The reinstatement was the first step toward Aiyuk's eventual release.

San Francisco drafted him with the 25th pick in the 2020 NFL Draft. He had his breakout season in 2022, finishing with 1,015 yards and eight touchdowns. Aiyuk returned in 2023 and improved, finishing with 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns.
