item.title: Washington Commanders officially sign Brandon Aiyuk to practice squad
item.description: The Commanders signed Brandon Aiyuk, former 49ers receiver and Jayden Daniels’ college teammate, to their practice squad
item.content:encoded:
UPDATE: The Commanders have officially announced the signing of receiver Brandon Aiyuk to their practice squad. They also added cornerback Ambry Thomas to the practice squad, and released receiver Malik Heath from the practice squad in a corresponding move.

It’s clear that Aiyuk will need some time to get used to the Commanders’ offensive system and to get into NFL game shape, and he’ll also need to help run the Washington scout team. His activation will come in time and try to help the Commanders down the stretch in their attempt to win the NFC East.

The Commanders have signed receiver Brandon Aiyuk to their practice squad, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday.  

The free agent, who was released by the San Francisco 49ers and formally cleared waivers, met with the Commanders at the team’s complex on Wednesday. Per Schefter, Aiyuk signed contract to join the team’s practice squad.  

This move was telegraphed somewhat, with the Tuesday release of running back Craig Reynolds to open up a spot.  

Aiyuk will have an opportunity to work himself back into game shape after more than two years on the shelf. The Commanders can elevate him when ready, or they can sign him to the active roster at a time of their choosing. He can be elevated three times before Washington has to formally activate him.  

Washington has been Aiyuk’s preferred destination, a point that was clear when he started wearing Commanders gear in social media posts over the summer.  

Some quick background: The 49ers drafted Aiyuk in the first round back in 2020 and then inked him to a four-year, $120-million contract in 2024.  

Then things got messy. Aiyuk suffered a serious knee injury during the 2024 campaign and didn’t play after that. The 49ers took issue with Aiyuk’s choice to rehab away from their facility, and it created a schism and a rift that was never repaired. The 49ers voided Aiyuk’s guarantees and placed him on the exempt/did not report list.  

Then Aiyuk went on a social media tirade, torching 49ers GM John Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan. He also took some shots at Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels – Aiyuk and Daniels were good friends and teammates at Arizona State – and his mother. They have reportedly mended fences, which set the stage for this signing.  

Commanders GM Adam Peters was also involved in the Aiyuk draft pick when he was in San Francisco.  

Aiyuk had 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns in 2023, shockingly his last full season in the NFL. There’s no doubting Aiyuk’s talent, though it has been some time since that has led to production.  

How long it takes for Aiyuk to get ready is to be determined, but Washington needs him to get prepared fast to keep this good thing going. It’s hard to imagine he’ll be ready for Sunday’s road game against the Arizona Cardinals, especially with his need to catch up learning the Commanders system. And there’s great shape and football shape, which are two totally different things.

Chiefs fans’ confidence

Whether fans’ overall confidence in the team stays as high as it is right now will depend on how the Chiefs perform at Highmark Stadium. I don’t think l the Chiefs have to win in order for fans to stay confident in the teams direction, but they do have to play well. If Kansas City’s pass rush looks ineffective or they make boneheaded errors on special teams, then fans are liable to lose a little bit of their gusto for this team’s direction.

But if KC comes out with their hair on fire and moves the ball well and play sound football, then win or lose I think most fans will feel okay about the team’s direction. I will say, one caveat to this is that the only teams the Chiefs have beaten with a winning record this season are the Broncos and the Raiders (at the time they played). At some point, you would like to see them beat a good team.

Can the Chiefs finally beat the Bills when it doesn’t matter?

There are a few reasons to be hopeful that the Kansas City Chiefs can walk out of Highmark Stadium with a victory on Thanksgiving night.

The Bills have allowed opposing teams to score 30 points or more on four different occasions this year.

The Chiefs have the second-best scoring defense, allowing just 16.3 points per game. The Chiefs also have the best red zone defense, allowing opposing teams to score a touchdown on just 36% of red zone visits.

Really, this game is going to come down to a few things.

  1. Can Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs keep up the offensive tear they have been on?
  2. Will Josh Allen make dumb decisions and turn the ball over? Allen already has 9 interceptions this season, compared to just 4 picks for Mahomes.
  3. Can Emmett Johnson continue to prove that he is the best offensive rookie in the NFL and run all over the Bills?
  4. Can the Chiefs stop Josh Allen from running the ball? You know it’s coming, but he is a big dude and not easy to bring down.

Bottom line, this is going to be a tough game and fingers crossed the good guys come out on top.

item.title: Blake Corum is the Rams’ best running back
item.description: He can’t take every snap, but he should be L.A.‘s featured back.
item.content:encoded:
Blake Corum was incredible for the Los Angeles Rams in their Week 12 win over the Green Bay Packers. He was nearly unstoppable as he gashed through the Green Bay defense, carrying the offense in a 26-13 victory.

Not only was Corum the best player in the game, he solidified himself as RB1 for the Rams going forward.

Los Angeles has the luxury of rotating between two starting-caliber running backs in Corum and Kyren Williams. If you don’t think that’s an enviable place to be, go look at the Rams’ opponents from Wednesday night, whose leading rusher was a wide receiver in a losing effort.

Williams has been a positive contributor for the Rams for years and still is right now. But when push came to shove in the biggest game of the season so far, Sean McVay put his faith in Corum.

Clearly, he was rewarded for his belief.

This season, Corum has tallied more yardage on fewer carries than Williams, and he was the go-to option in a game the Rams truly could not afford to lose. The third-year pro posted 33 carries for 184 yards in the win over the Packers; that’s the highest number of carries for a Ram since Zac Stacy in 2013, and it’s the most single-game yardage for a Ram since Todd Gurley in 2018.

It should be noted that Corum was doing this behind a depleted offensive line, too, with a pair of starters out (not to mention the holes due to injury across the rest of the offensive roster). Part of that is the Packers’ porous run defense, which has now given up the two highest individual rushing totals of the season, but still, it’s not as if he had wide-open running lanes all night. According to Next Gen Stats, Corum had 150 yards after contact on Wednesday night.

There’s something to be said for riding the hot hand, and that’s definitely part of what went into Wednesday’s Corum-heavy second half. After all, Ronnie Rivers had a turn being the workhorse last time out in a win over the Arizona Cardinals.

But this is back-to-back weeks that Corum has out-touched Williams. And, as mentioned above, his full-season stats have been even more efficient while scoring at a nearly identical clip (Corum has six rushing touchdowns, Williams has seven after Week 12).

Williams should still play plenty of snaps down the stretch, obviously. He’s still a good player, it’s not like he’s chopped liver compared to Corum. And by splitting the snaps between two backs, you’re ideally keeping both a bit fresher for a potential postseason run. Just ask the Seattle Seahawks and Kenneth Walker III about how much of a boon it is to have a fresh running back in January and February.

But as things stand today, the best running back the Rams have is Blake Corum. For a running game that is not just efficient but can also completely take over a game like we just saw, the focal point right now should be Corum, no matter what the other back in the rotation has accomplished before.

item.content:encoded:
Happy Thanksgiving weekend, everybody. While the rest of us are going to enjoy some days with family and food, the NFL is quite busy: a total of 16 games will be played between Wednesday and Monday, with at least one game on on five of the next six days.

One of those will be played by the New England Patriots, who are going to take on the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET. There are no questions about who to root for in this specific game, but how about the others? Let’s take a look.

Once again, a quick explainer: as long as the Patriots are still theoretically alive in the race for a playoff spot, we will root with that possibility in mind.

Thursday

1 p.m. ET

Chicago Bears (8-2) at Detroit Lions (8-2): Go good game! The Patriots lost to both teams already this year, so this really makes no difference whatsoever. | CBS

4:30 p.m. ET

Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) at Dallas Cowboys (5-6): Go good game! Two NFC East rivals going against one another with no impact on the Patriots. Time to enjoy a second slice of pie. | FOX

8:20 p.m. ET

Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) at Buffalo Bills (9-1): Go… Bills? Okay, stay with us here. If we are being honest with ourselves, the Patriots can probably kiss their dreams of defending the AFC East title this season goodbye. However, the playoffs are still a possibility. Other teams are more realistic candidates to drop behind New England — looking at you, Pittsburgh — but if the Chiefs have no games on their schedule where it would be essential for us to root for rather than against them. So, in an ideal scenario, they kick off a losing streak on Thursday night that might just allow the Patriots to overtake them further down the road. Of course, the chances of that actually happening are fairly low, but one can dream. | NBC

Friday

3 p.m. ET

Denver Broncos (8-2) at Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4): Go Broncos! Now this is a game that truly matters. The Steelers are the current seventh seed in the AFC and as such the Patriots’ closest rival in the race for a postseason spot. In fact, if they lose to the Broncos and New England wins in L.A. then the Patriots are suddenly ahead of them in the standings. Luckily for the Patriots, the Steelers are doing their best these days to at least play their part in that. | Prime Video

Sunday

1 p.m. ET

New Orleans Saints (3-7) at Cincinnati Bengals (7-3): Go Saints! Somebody has to win the AFC North, and the Bengals are the best bet right now. That said, it would be good if they had to fight for playoff positioning until the very last week of the season, just in case the Patriots need them to beat the Browns in Week 18. With. that in mind, we are rooting for the Saints in this one. | CBS

Baltimore Ravens (4-7) at Houston Texans (4-6): Go Ravens! Another somewhat important game from a Patriots point of view. Neither team is currently in the playoff picture, but the Texans have seemingly started hitting their stride and a loss to the moribund Ravens would help break their momentum and make a late push harder. | CBS

New York Giants (6-3-1) at Indianapolis Colts (3-8): Go Colts! Indianapolis entering the playoff race seems like a long shot, meaning that this can be a game where we root with draft position in mind. Don’t forget: the Jets earn the Colts’ first-rounder next year. | FOX

Tennessee Titans (1-9) at Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3): Go Titans! With games against the Steelers and Texans still on their schedule, the Patriots will want the Jaguars to have to bring their A-game in both contests. Maybe some heat applied from a loss to their division rivals can help with that. | FOX

New York Jets (3-8) at Miami Dolphins (1-9): Go Dolphins! We are rooting for the worse-positioned AFC East team in this one, once again from a draft perspective. | CBS

Atlanta Falcons (3-7) at Minnesota Vikings (7-3): Go Vikings! Four words: strength of schedule tiebreaker. Will it matter? Unlikely. Is it better to be safe than sorry, though? Absolutely. | FOX

New England has a clear edge over Las Vegas, but is looking up in the standings to the Browns. 32. Mason Rudolph (vs. DEN) - 9.8 proj. points

Week 12 TE Rankings

1. Trey McBride (vs. WAS) - 59.5 proj. yards

McBride is going to be just fine. Josh Johnson was a checkdown artist all Week 11 against the Chiefs, and McBride was still trying to hurdle defenders and work his butt off. The Cardinals have nowhere else to go in the pass game, and they're going to be in huge negative scripts the rest of the way. He'll lead the position in targets by a comfortable margin. Touchdowns will be hard to come by, but that's okay.

The matchup is great. The Commanders will blitz and leave underneath gaps behind it for McBride. Washington has allowed the second-most fantasy points to TEs, including 77 yards to Mike Gesicki on Monday Night Football. Isaiah Likely has been the TE1 overall in each of his games against them. It's the same role in the offense here.

2. Brock Bowers (at CLE) - 66.5 proj. yards

We'll see how much he practices this week.

3. Colston Loveland (at DET) - 52.5 proj. yards

Loveland is the TE5 on TE4 usage since Caleb Williams returned in Week 6. He's averaging 7.5 targets over the past month and hurdled a defender for a score last week as a full-time player.

This is a great matchup for Loveland. The Bears project for the third-most points, and the Lions are without LB Jack Campbell amongst others. They've allowed the most half PPR points to the position (17.4 per game), and Loveland had 91-1 against them in Week 18 of last year himself.

4. Isaiah Likely (at IND) - 50.5 proj. yards

Likely is the TE2 on TE3 overall this year, averaging 8.1 targets per game despite largely leading games. He's simply that important to the offense, essentially operating as a bigger Wan'Dale Robinson. Last week's dud was defense- and game-script related. I'm not worried about it.

The Colts are tanking and have been shredded due to inexperienced LB play. The Giants travel as 6.5-point road favorites, carrying a 24-point implied team total (10th). It's a good spot for Likely.

5. T.J. Hockenson (vs. ATL) - 44.5 proj. yards

Hockenson is benefiting from the Kirk Cousins trade and the Jordan Addison injury. He is the TE8 on TE6 usage over his last four games, seeing between 7.6 and 10.1 expected half PPR points in all four contests. He's a stable low-end TE1 option.

Atlanta ranks 14th in half PPR points allowed to tight ends at 10.9 points per game. It's been better against the position of late, but it's without FS Jessie Bates III now. Minnesota enters as 7-point home favorites with an implied team total of 24.25 points (eighth).

6. George Kittle (vs. SEA) - 46.5 proj. yards

Kittle is the TE4 on TE4 usage this season. His involvement could take a slight hit with Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. healthy and Keenan Allen added to the lineup, but there are few with more big-play ability, despite being 33 years old coming off a torn Achilles. Just ask the Vikings, who were TE eliminators before Kittle finished as the TE2 overall with a pair of scores. Incredible.

Seattle ranks 27th in half PPR points allowed to tight ends at 8.1 per game, though they did give up 65 yards to Colston Loveland in Week 8. Kittle has had less luck against them, finishing with 24, 29 and 25 yards in his games, respectively, since S/LB Nick Emmanwori showed up. San Francisco enters as 3-point home favorites with a 25.25-point implied team total (eighth). It's a tough spot for Kittle. I'm just not going to ever doubt him.

7. Harold Fannin Jr. (vs. LV) - 49.5 proj. yards

Fannin ranks as the TE2 on TE4 usage over his last four games, the best stretch of his sophomore season. Head coach Todd Monken has recently stated that they have to keep him very involved after not throwing him a screen for the first six weeks of the year. Bizarre! He still has some of the best YAC moments in the NFL, not at his position. All positions. Fannin has drawn at least nine targets in three of his last four outings. What a star.

The Raiders present a generous spot, ranking fifth in half PPR points allowed to tight ends with 13.4 per game. Las Vegas conceded 74 yards on eight targets to Evan Engram (!!!) last week, along with a four-catch, 58-yard finish to George Kittle in Week 9. Cleveland enters the matchup as 4.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 23 points (15th).

8. Travis Kelce (at BUF) - 46.5 proj. yards

Kelce sits as the TE3 on TE8 usage over his last four games, averaging 12.7 half PPR points on 8.4 expected points per game. He bounced back from a two-target outing in Week 10 with a season-high 22.4 half PPR points against Arizona in Week 11, catching 6-of-7 targets for 74 yards and two touchdowns alongside a season-high 58 air yards.

The Bills are a good matchup for Kelce, not because they are a bad defense. It's that they are better at stopping the run than the pass, and because the Chiefs are actually underdogs. More dropbacks than normal wouldn't be a surprise, and the weather calls for some rain and wind, likely meaning more underneath passes than anything deep. Kelce has 66, 19, 8, 75, 83 and 112 yards, respectively, against Buffalo since 2022, for what it's worth. Kansas City heads on the road as 3-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 23.75 points (11th). He'll see SS Cole Bishop in the box plenty. It'll be an even matchup there.

9. Sam LaPorta (vs. CHI) - 44.5 proj. yards

It's been a quiet year for LaPorta, but he was able to find space a couple of times against the Bucs for explosives, finishing as the TE12 on TE8 usage. Across the year, he's the TE7 on TE5 usage, though most of that came before Week 6. He's only the TE29 on TE11 usage this past month. With all Lions, it's best to take the largest sample. There are more mouths than targets to go around, so somebody will get left behind at times. He can get hot at any time.

Chicago ranks 24th in half PPR points allowed to opposing tight ends, yielding 8.7 points per game. Across their last three games with DT Jeffery Simmons in-house, the Bears have given up 4.5 points or fewer to opposing TE rooms, though that's the Saints, Bucs and Seahawks. LaPorta has been the TE31, TE5 and TE8 against them most recently. Detroit enters as 2.5-point home underdogs with an implied team total of 26.5 points (sixth). He'll need a touchdown to pay off.

10. Brenton Strange (vs. TEN) - 32.5 proj. yards

The volume is not there (4.2 targets per game), but Strange is a TD threat at any moment. With the Titans tanking, it's a great spot to hope for a score or two. The Jaguars project for 31.0 points. Tennessee has allowed 361.8 passing yards per game this month. That boggles the mind. Strange has also been the TE11, TE5 and TE5 against them most recently.

11. Chig Okonkwo (at ARI) - 38.5 proj. yards

12. Tyler Warren (vs. NYG) - 27.5 proj. yards

Warren is not making enough plays in the pass game. He's not a loose athlete, rather trying to overpower or win in a straight line. That's a missing trait versus the truly elite TEs across the league. He's more of a Diet Coke Tucker Kraft than a Trey McBride type. His situation is getting harder to trust, too, with Anthony Richardson Sr. stepping into the starting lineup. We seriously don't even know how well he can see!!! He's also a threat to steal goal-line scores and wants to launch the ball well over the head of Warren's typical target depth. The Colts host the Giants as 6.5-point home underdogs with an implied team total of 17.5 points (29th).

13. Tucker Kraft (at LAR) - 37.5 proj. yards

Kraft is a distant third option in the pass game. He's only the TE15 on TE8 usage this season thanks to some untimely drops and a huge regression in the yards after catch department. Predictably so. He's too talented to not have a couple of big games down the stretch, but he's been on the TE1/2 border all year. There's no reason to change that now.

The Rams have been stingy against tight ends, ranking 29th with 8.0 half PPR points allowed per game. They've faced Trey McBride twice (37 and 53 scoreless yards) and Brock Bowers (73 scoreless), too. Green Bay heads into the matchup as 3-point road underdogs carrying an implied team total of 20.75 points (19th).

14. Tyler Higbee (vs. GB) - 29.5 proj. yards

Higbee is a nice streaming option for those in TE trouble. The Rams used formations rarely used in Week 10 without their top-2 WRs, but we'll see if they stick with those after the bye in a game expected to be a lot closer than the Cardinals blowout. It'd make sense for the Rams to use plenty of 3-TE looks, and Higbee is the loosest athlete of the bunch when in them. Even as a part-time player in Week 10, Higbee had four targets on nine routes. Two of them were in the end zone on first-read looks. I think there's more upside here than what his recent box scores would suggest.

The Packers have been very good at defending TEs for a couple of reasons. One: they have awesome safeties; two: they have a lot of chaotic pre-snap looks that sometimes keep TEs in to block. The Rams are more equipped to beat them, especially with a bye week to prepare.

15. Dalton Kincaid (vs. KC) - 38.5 proj. yards

Kincaid said he's playing, but he's only been limited with thumb and ankle injuries on the official report. He's likely not fully healthy, but this game is big enough to push to play after taking a week off. There will be rainy and windy conditions to fight through, so there's a really low floor just if they want to run the ball in heavier sets. His ankle could also be impacted by the sloppy field conditions, too. Kincaid has been the TE9 on TE14 usage this year with no rhyme or reason for when he's going to have a random big game. I'd love to hear Kincaid theories if you have them!

Kansas City's defense represents a run-funnel tendency, as opponents have thrown on just 46% of neutral plays against them, the lowest in the NFL. That said, when teams pass, the ball can get funneled to TEs. They've allowed the seventh-most half PPR points to the position, with both Brock Bowers (TE2 overall) and Trey McBride (TE7) doing their thing recently. Part of it is that they have two stud outside CBs to slow down WRs, while being more mediocre up the spine. Buffalo enters Thanksgiving as 3-point home favorites with an implied total of 26.75 points (fifth). For what it's worth, Kincaid popped off for 101 yards in Week 9 of last year against this defense.

item.content:encoded:
Week 12 of the NFL season kicked off with a rare Wednesday matchup between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, prepping us for a full Thanksgiving feast of football the following day, headlined by an MVP showcase between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs on Thursday night.

Ahead of that matchup, the Steelers made headlines by reportedly benching veteran quarterback and former MVP Aaron Rodgers in favor of backup Mason Rudolph for Week 12 after recent struggles on offense.

This storyline then reached a fever pitch on Wednesday when Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" and went scorched-earth on a rant about head coach Mike McCarthy. Rodgers accused McCarthy of repeatedly falling asleep in meetings and ending a team breakdown with "1-2-3 Let's go Packers."

Shortly after his appearance on the show, the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac reported that Rodgers was being released. The quarterback had said on the show that he was "not going back to Pittsburgh." He was officially waived on Wednesday afternoon's transaction wire.

We're watching plenty of injuries ahead of the action, including Las Vegas Raiders All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers, who missed Week 11 with an ankle injury, though he was reportedly pushing to play in that matchup. The Kansas City Chiefs have already ruled out running back Kenneth Walker III for his third consecutive game with a groin injury, giving rookie Emmett Johnson the nod for a Thanksgiving contest with the Buffalo Bills.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest NFL news, injury updates and more coming out of Week 11.

item.title: The Lions, despite their resurgence, are 1-8 in their last nine Thanksgiving games
item.description: The Lions commenced their ongoing resurgence in 2022.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions commenced their ongoing resurgence in 2022. That hasn't translated to sustained success on Thanksgiving.

They're 1-8 over the last nine Thanksgiving Day games.

The one win in that stretch came two years ago, against the Bears. That day, Chicago pocketed a timeout as the final 30 seconds or so ticked away, leaving the Bears without enough time to attempt a field goal that would have forced overtime in a 23-20 game.

The next day, the Bears fired coach Matt Eberflus. It paved the way for the eventual hiring of Lions offensive coordinator Ben Johnson, who returns to Ford Field today for the second time.

Last year's game didn't go very well. Detroit scored 52 points. The Bears lost the Soldier Field rematch, too.

This year, history takes a back seat to the immediate future. Both the Bears and the Lions are 8-2. The Lions have won all six of their home games. The winner takes control, for now, of the NFC North — and stays within striking distance of the 9-1 49ers for the No. 1 seed.

It's not hyperbole to call it the most significant early-window Thanksgiving game ever. In many years, the Lions were the punching bag on turkey day. They're now the ones doing the punching.

Which makes the 1-8 trend even more surprising.

For the Bears, the challenge is to prove that they're Super Bowl contenders. They entered the discussion with their Week 8 Monday night win in Seattle. Today, the Bears have a chance to control the narrative.

However it goes, the numbers should be eye-popping. For last year's Packers-Lions game, 47.7 million tuned in. It was a new all-time regular-season record audience, until Chiefs-Cowboys later that day shattered it with 57.23 million viewers.

All three games could be compelling today. Eagles-Cowboys got a boost from both teams winning on Sunday. And Chiefs-Bills continues to be one of the top rivalries in the league — even if cold and wind and rain could take more than a little steam out of the offenses.

Enjoy the day. We'll be here throughout the games, posting all relevant updates and other NFL news. It's a privilege, not a burden, to spend time on Thanksgiving doing what we always do. And we're thankful for the fact that you choose to consume it.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers’ grim NFL reality revealed after explosive interview
item.description: The Steelers released Aaron Rodgers after he criticized coach Mike McCarthy, a move Adam Schefter believes marks the end of the QB's career.
item.content:encoded:
ESPN insider Adam Schefter said Aaron Rodgers knew his career was over and tried to take Mike McCarthy down with him after the quarterback unleashed serious allegations against his now former head coach on Wednesday’s installment of “The Pat McAfee Show.”

After the Steelers announced Tuesday night that Rodgers would be inactive against Denver this week, Rodgers did a surprise TV appearance and accused McCarthy of sleeping during team meetings.

He also said McCarthy missed a walk-through Friday and a meeting Saturday morning before the Steelers’ 19-16 loss to the Eagles on Sunday. Rodgers was released Wednesday shortly after the interview.

During a WEEI radio appearance, Schefter called Rodgers’ takedown of McCarthy “unprecedented” and painted a bleak picture of the quarterback’s playing future.

“Look, in this league anything is always possible and there could be a team that decides that its quarterback play is deficient enough that it needs to bring in Aaron Rodgers,” Schefter said when asked if the Patriots, who are without injured starter Drake Maye for the foreseeable future, could be a landing spot for Rodgers.

“But, my guess, just a guess. Texted a couple GMs today. I think that he knew his career was over and he tried to end Mike McCarthy’s career as well. Two guys going down together today. That was my sense of it. Now could somebody give him a shot, sure. I’m not expecting that. Do you think a team is gonna roll out and go sign him after that?”

Schefter explained that Rodgers — a four-time NFL MVP and Super Bowl champ, who turns 43 next week — at this point in his career, didn’t care about the ramifications of torching McCarthy on-air.

“And he doesn’t care. He’s had an unbelievable career. He’s one of the greatest players to ever play. He’s made more money than he can ever spend,” Schefter said. “So he doesn’t care.”

“For him to take down the head coach like that and embarrass him, it doesn’t matter to him… By the way, it’s not like there was a robust market for his services before this. And after this I don’t think that that helps his cause with other teams.”

During his appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show,” Rodgers challenged the Steelers to release him if changes weren’t implemented — and they took him up on his offer after his shocking interview.

McCarthy, who spoke to the media hours after Rodgers’ interview, did not directly confirm or deny sleeping in meetings.

The coach did admit another allegation made by Rodgers, that he mistakenly said, “1-2-3 Packers!” in a team huddle during Sunday’s loss in Philadelphia.

McCarthy said it was an “embarrassing moment” and explained that working “long hours” was a factor in the slip-up.

He added that he spoke with his players and had a “very direct and very honest” meeting.

“I appreciated the opportunity to talk through numerous things that have been on their mind,” McCarthy said, adding that the conversation should have happened sooner.

It’s unclear where Rodgers’ career goes from here.

The quarterback previously said this is his final season after returning to Pittsburgh on a one-year, $22.5 million contract.

One AFC team executive told ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, “Teams desperate on the playoff bubble, maybe, but it’s going to be hard after watching him go scorched earth on people and an organization like that.”

The Steelers hired McCarthy in January after Rodgers pushed for the coach to get an interview with the team following Mike Tomlin’s departure.

item.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' RB Blueprint for Week 12
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks lays out the blueprint for the RB position for Week 12.
item.content:encoded:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be this RB column, a WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available here.

1. Jahmyr Gibbs (vs. CHI) - 132.5 proj. total yards

Gibbs has recently finished as the RB5 and RB3 against the Vikings and Bucs, respectively, both defenses that sit at the top of every fantasy RB metric. There's no stopping this train.

The Bears defense is much better with DT Jeffery Simmons wreaking havoc, but Gibbs has shredded this defense for 100+ total yards in 4 straight games. Detroit enters as 2.5-point home underdogs with a 26.5-point implied total (sixth). Don't be surprised if his receiving volume ticks up here.

2. Emmett Johnson (at BUF) - 116.5 proj. total yards

With Kenneth Walker III (groin) ruled out again, this time for Thursday night's game against the Bills, Johnson remains a top-five play. The rookie popped off for RB3 and RB6 finishes the last two games, handling the usual Kenneth Walker III role. He reminds me of Bucky Irving in some ways, but there is still a physicality and long-speed gap to Walker.

Long term, Johnson will return to his part time role, perhaps with an extra handful of reps, but he's set for another heavy workload this week. The matchup is more mediocre. The Bills' defense is coming alive in Year 1 of a new system, thanks to a trade at the deadline for a safety and a few breakouts up front. They're middle of the pack in most metrics, and the Chiefs are only projected for 23.25 points (13th) as field-goal dogs.

3. Bucky Irving (vs. CAR) - 102.5 proj. total yards

Irving has been fantastic since the end of September. He's been the RB5 on RB3 usage this past month, hulking 22.3 carries per game. Last week was another great outing, despite having an 80-yard TD called back for a rightful holding. Irving is the engine of the offense with the pass game completely broken for QB and WR reasons.

The Panthers are still poor stopping the run despite a DC change. They allowed Derrick Henry to go for 111 total yards and a score, and across the season Carolina is second-worst against the position. Irving hit them for 110-2 back in Week 7 (RB2) with RB18, RB41, RB5 and RB1 finishes in previous years. It's a great spot all around. The Bucs project for 23.25 points (13th) in a must-win game in the NFC South.

4. Christian McCaffrey (vs. SEA) - 88.5 proj. total yards

McCaffrey is a patriot. He's posted RB22 and RB14 outings outside of the states but is the RB2 on RB6 usage inside the country. CMC will play the rest of his games in the USA for those tracking at home. There's nothing new with his role or production. He's the RB3 this season thanks to his usual receiving role (RB4 in receptions per game) and the 49ers' truly dominant scoring offense.

Seattle will be a real test, just like the Vikings were last week. Seattle sits 24th in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields, and the Seahawks are fresh off a bye week. CMC was the RB11 with 83 total yards against them in Week 5 when the Niners won 32 to 29. He had 74, 57 and 142 scoreless yards against them in last year's matchups, too. It's reasonable to dock him for matchup reasons, but only so much. The 49ers dictate terms this year. San Francisco heads in as 3-point home favorites carrying a 25.25-point implied team total (eighth).

5. Bijan Robinson (at MIN) - 99.5 proj. total yards

I'm afraid a real reset is due. Bijan has been the RB11 on RB10 usage over the past month, sinking against the 49ers (RB19) and Bucs (RB28) with Michael Penix forgetting how to play QB. He's still handling a major workload and is too good not to have huge games down the stretch, but the Falcons did trade away their starting C and really struggling on defense, too.

This week, the Falcons are firmly in the "mid" quadrant. They're projected for just 17.5 points (28th) as touchdown dogs to the Vikings. Minnesota is obviously one of the best defenses, even if the Niners did whatever they wanted to last week. Penix's pressure panic could derail the entire offense if they aren't prepared. The plan will be to run the ball against them while they can, but hopefully it's not just a punt fest. The Vikings have recently faced a bunch of fantasy RB1s; Christian McCaffrey (RB15), James Cook (RB7), Jahmyr Gibbs (RB5) and Jonathan Taylor (RB8). Taking the average of that group would be an optimistic angle, as Atlanta is nowhere near as good as those offenses.

6. Cam Skattebo (at IND) - 95.5 proj. total yards

Skattebo dominated touches again. He had 14 carries and seven targets in an upset win against the Jaguars, leading to 17.0 expected half PPR points. Despite fumbling in the second half, the Giants stuck with him and he ultimately closed the game out with a backflip. It's almost as simple as they don't want Devin Singletary on the field anymore, which means Skattebo should float to some nice RB1/2 weeks.

The bad news is his tape last week was pretty rough, as was J.J. McCarthy's. They won't face a loaded Jaguars defense every week, but Skattebo is at risk of being benched if he continues to put the ball on the dirt. His range of outcomes remains wide, but there is clear upside if he can keep it together.

This is a matchup to feel confident in with the Colts very clearly tanking. They've allowed 26.5 half PPR points to RB rooms over their past four games, on 152 rushing YPG. David Montgomery had 124 total yards, Ollie Gordon had 115, Javonte Williams had 124 and Bhayshul Tuten had 159. This is a blowup spot with the Giants projected for 24.0 points.

7. Jonah Coleman (at PIT) - 100.5 proj. total yards

Coleman has completely dusted J.K. Dobbins, who had one snap in Week 11's blowout win. His vision is what stands out on tape. He knows when to cut back, find cheap yards and bounce it depending on the look. He's a pretty mediocre athlete, but Coleman will hit a ton of singles and doubles behind this quality OL and rushing scheme.

Jonah Coleman has very good vision. Going to be one of the better singles and doubles hitters. pic.twitter.com/JesVhyUioV

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 23, 2026

On top of that, Coleman is averaging 3.5 receptions per game this month with R.J. Harvey out of the way. He's been the RB2, RB9 and RB7 in usage most recently. Look at the names he's next to here:

The matchup is far more difficult this week, however, after beating up on the Panthers and Raiders. The Steelers are a full tier above those DLs, even if they are pretty banged up at the moment. They haven't allowed a 100-yard back in more than six weeks. Saquon Barkley (RB13) and Chase Brown (RB6) scored their way to nice games most recently, for what it's worth. Denver has a 20.25-point team total (21st).

8. Javonte Williams (vs. PHI) - 88.5 proj. total yards

Williams is the RB8 on RB5 usage, riding the coattails of an amazing Dak Prescott season. He's easily leading the NFL in goal-line carries, and the Cowboys OL is one of the best. It's a great environment for fantasy points, that's for sure.

This week is no different. The Eagles traded away run-stopping DT Jordan Davis, placed All Pro LB Zack Baun on IR and won't have others on defense. It's a tanking defense that is now allowing 121 rushing YPG (12th most). Williams has already hit them for 155 total yards and a score this year back in Week 7, after finishing as the RB19 and RB3, respectively, against a better version of this defense in 2025. The Cowboys own a 28.0-point team total (fourth) on Thanksgiving as massive favorites.

9. James Cook III (vs. KC) - 98.5 proj. total yards

There is some serious weather expected here. Very cold rain with wind.

Cook sits as the RB9 in half PPR points per game on RB8 usage across his last four games. He leads the league with 23 carries per game in that span and has found the end zone on the ground in 4 straight contests. Nothing new here.

The matchup is an uphill one. Kansas City ranks 28th in half PPR points allowed to RBs, albeit with a fairly soft schedule so far. They did hold Bijan Robinson to RB13 a couple of weeks ago, for what it's worth. Offenses facing the Chiefs have attempted to run on them in neutral situations (league-low 46% neutral pass), and the Bills have the personnel to do that. Cook has had 125 and 134 total yards against the Chiefs in his most recent outings, respectively. Buffalo carries a 26.75-point implied total (fifth) as 3-point home favorites. I'm not adjusting too much for matchup.

10. Chris Rodriguez (vs. TEN)

We'll see if Bhayshul Tuten (ankle) going to keep playing through this ankle/foot injury, but he was a DNP on Wednesday and coach Liam Coen’s comments suggest they might sit him. The Jaguars project for 32.0 points (1st), so Rodriguez is a clear-cut RB1.

11. Chuba Hubbard (at TB) - 90.5 proj. total yards

Fantasy's MVP (Most Valuable Pick) without a doubt. Hubbard is the RB4 on RB4 usage this year, and the Panthers have rode him extra hard this past month (RB1 overall usage). He's the only stable part of their offense.

The Buccaneers represent the league's toughest positional test on paper, ranking 32nd in half PPR points allowed to RBs at 14.8 per game. Opposing backfields generate just 9.8 rushing points per game against Tampa Bay (29th), though Jahmyr Gibbs did post an RB3 finish against them in Week 11 in what I'd call a true bat fight. Hubbard was held to 60 scoreless yards in Week 7 and hasn't finished better than RB24 against them since Week 13 of 2023. Carolina heads on the road as 3-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 20.25 points (21st). Without question, this is a difficult spot.

12. D'Andre Swift (at DET) - 66.5 proj. total yards

Swift had a rough game on tape and lost meaningful touches to others in the backfield. He bounced a zone run that should've been cut back, then proceeded to fumble. He didn't return after that rep in the fourth quarter. That said, the Kyle Monangai tape was lackluster, too. He's not 100% on his right toe injury and will have a short week with Thanksgiving here. The assumption is Swift starts, leads the backfield and doesn't have the RB1 role he had without Monangai. Since Week 5 of last year, Swift is the RB14 on RB16 usage. He was the RB16 on RB16 usage last week. View him as a boom-bust RB2.

The Lions defense is going to miss DE Aidan Hutchinson and LB Jack Campbell, though they still have some physical DEs and star DTs to worry about up front. Across the year, the Lions are fourth-best against fantasy RBs, but with the recent injuries and the fact that the Bears can stay in positive game scripts, this Lions defense seems more vulnerable than the spreadsheets would indicate. They have put a lid on Swift's fantasy value in recent matchups, for what it's worth, as Swift has mounted 48, 69, 53 and 74 yards, respectively, against them since 2024. A massive 29.0-point team total (third) is the most important mark, however. There is plenty of upside.

13. Kyren Williams (vs. GB) - 80.5 proj. total yards

Williams has had his two worst fantasy games of the year in back-to-back weeks. In Week 10 before the bye, Blake Corum outclassed him as a ball carrier, simply showcasing more short-area burst while offering the same high-level vision. The Rams also made sure to say Williams has a "sore toe", which, in a worst-case scenario, would be a turf toe. That's a terrible injury for a RB to try to play through. We're finally at the point that Corum has a chance to steal more carries from Williams, who is likely to remain the favorite in the pass game if the Rams are ever trailing. Even over this "bad" month stretch, Williams is the RB17 in expected half PPR points.

The Packers have been run on at times, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to RBs. They're on a 6-game stretch of allowing a top-20 fantasy RB and have missed LB Edgerrin Cooper (Achilles). We'll see if Micah Parsons (ACL) is playing, as expected. While 3-point favorites, the Rams "only" project for 23.75 points (12th) this week. Williams is a suddenly volatile fantasy RB2.

14. Blake Corum (vs. GB) - 71.5 proj. total yards

To my eyes and the spreadsheet's charts, Corum is a better rusher than Kyren Williams, who is reportedly dealing with a "sore toe" coming out of the bye. It'd be a bit of a surprise if Corum was the early-down starter, but I'm open to it happening for the first time ever. Corum won't have the pass-game value that Williams has shown off, but he's still the RB12 on RB20 usage this past month with the offense losing Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. They really need the Corum explosive runs to keep the offense alive.

The Packers have been run on at times, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to RBs. They're on a 6-game stretch of allowing a top-20 fantasy RB and have missed LB Edgerrin Cooper (Achilles). We'll see if Micah Parsons (ACL) is playing, as expected. While 3-point favorites, the Rams "only" project for 23.75 points (12th) this week. Corum can be viewed as a fantasy RB2 in the same tier as Williams.

15. Breece Hall (at MIA) - 78.5 proj. total yards

Hall played on 5-of-6 snaps inside the 10-yard line last week, so it's not as cut-and-dry as Braelon Allen is The Biggest, The Largest and will be subbed in for all red-zone work. Since returning from injury, Hall is the RB13 on RB15 usage. He had his best game last week in a win, while finishing as an RB2/FLEX in losses to the Chiefs and Bills. The Jets want to run the ball as much as they can, but the game script will need to cooperate to pull that off.

Enter the Dolphins. The Jets are favored, and Miami has allowed the 7th-most fantasy points to RBs this year. They've also recently placed three key DTs on injured reserve. James Cook just finished as the RB10 against them last week, and they've been on a 6-game streak of allowing at least one RB to finish as a top-24 back. It's a good spot of course.

16. Chase Brown (vs. NO) - 73.5 proj. total yards

That was a painful primetime game from Brown, who dropped multiple targets and took 6 carries for just 6 yards. He's the RB21 on RB15 usage this season, as one of the most inefficient players with the context of how great this Bengals offense is. I'm not sure if he's even better than Samaje Perine, who is one of the most underrated insurance options as we close out the fantasy season. This offense gives Brown multi-score upside as we saw in Week 10, but those were out of structure receiving touchdowns. Perine threatens at the goal line and now in the 2-minute drill. He's a volatile fantasy RB2, as he's been throughout the year. Brown is leading the position in receptions per game (5.2).

The Saints offer one of the friendliest matchups in football, ranking 2nd in half PPR points allowed to running backs at 25.6 points per game. New Orleans ranks 3rd in rushing points allowed (18.4 per game) and 8th in receiving points allowed to the position, having recently surrendered big games to Chuba Hubbard (RB4) and Jaylen Warren (RB17). Cincinnati features the league's highest neutral pass rate at 67% (1st) and enters as 10-point home favorites with an implied total of 30.75 points (2nd).

17. Saquon Barkley (at DAL) - 76.5 proj. total yards

We'll see if Barkley is going to play after his second stinger of the season last week ...

Barkley hit the gas last week and still looks like one of the best backs on tape. That's the good news. The problem is he was still only the RB13 on RB21 usage, without a reception, in an offense that is absolutely stuck with bad QB play. He only played 64% of the snaps coming out of the bye, losing some pass-game work to Will Shipley. He'll need a big play and some infrequent goal-line scores to hold the line as a fantasy RB2. He's the RB19 on RB36 usage since returning. Consider that his low-end baseline.

The reason for hope here is the Cowboys defense. They were hilarious against the Titans last week and have allowed the most fantasy points to RBs (25.7 half PPR per game) throughout the year on the most rushing yards per game (152). It's somehow been worse over their past month (31.1 PG). Barkley had a couple of impressive reps when returning from injury against them in Week 7 (RB20 on RB32 usage) and is in a better spot now. Philadelphia enters the holiday matchup as 8.5-point road underdogs with an implied total of 19.5 points (23rd). He has to take over for the Eagles to pull off the upset.

18. Derrick Henry (at HOU) - 65.5 proj. total yards

The last two games with Jacoby Brissett have been totally fine. He's been the RB9 and RB12 on RB12 and RB11 usage. That's a good baseline for him moving forward, but we'll have to adjust for matchup as those games were close games against the Chargers and Panthers. He's catching more passes in an offense that will add 10+ dropbacks per game versus previous versions of this offense. That will offset the potential drop in goal line scores.

Houston ranks 19th in half PPR points allowed to running backs this season (18.5 per game), including a 20th-place ranking in rushing fantasy points surrendered to the position. The Texans recently held Jonathan Taylor to an RB33 finish in Week 11 after yielding an RB15 showing to Quinshon Judkins in Week 10. They won't have LB Azeez Al-Shair but have a strong DL still. Baltimore enters as 6.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 20 points (22nd).

19. Tony Pollard (at JAX) - 79.5 proj. total yards

Pollard has been carrying the Titans offense, one that is playing at the league's fastest pace over the past month to better fit Cam Ward's chaotic skillset. More play volume is always welcomed for fantasy. Pollard has been the RB3 on RB7 usage over that stretch, handling 19.0 carries and 3.5 receptions per game. Tyjae Spears is on IR, so it's strictly Pollard until absolute garbage time. At any point, the Titans can completely disintegrate on offense without LG Peter Skoronski. He's best viewed as fantasy RB2 even if the results have been better than that of late.

The Jaguars have an awesome defense. Pollard broke a few tackles on a checkdown for a long score against them two games ago, finishing as the RB8 on RB12 usage. That's as good of an outcome as we can hope for. Since then, they've added two quality starters, including run-stopping DT Jordan Davis. Across the year, Jacksonville has allowed the 3rd-fewest fantasy points to RBs (15.1 half PPR per game). Pollard was the RB25 and RB47 against them last year, and they haven't allowed a 100-yard RB this season and only two have cleared 14 carries. Opposing backfields muster just 8.7 rushing fantasy points per game (30th) against the Jaguars, prompting offenses facing them to pass at a 59% rate in neutral scripts (second-highest). Tennessee travels as 14.5-point road underdogs with a slate-low implied team total of 16.5 points (32nd).

20. Jonathan Taylor (vs. NYG) - 87.5 proj. total yards

There's a ton going on. The Colts releasing Daniel Jones for Anthony Richardson Sr. is a slight negative for Taylor, as ARich is more likely to score near the goal line and less likely to maintain long drives. Indianapolis also didn't have its starting OTs last week (and of course, it traded LG Quenton Nelson) and Richardson's play under pressure is concerning. That's something very much worth tracking. As a reminder, here are Taylor's historical splits based on how many points Indy scores:

Jonathan Taylor fantasy points since 2021:
+ Colts score 0-17 ➡️ 11.3 half PPR (RB18)
+ Colts score 18-24 ➡️ 14.9 (RB15)
+ Colts score 25-30 ➡️ 19.7 (RB3)
+ Colts score 31+ ➡️ 29.5 (RB1)

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 10, 2026

The Colts project for 17.5 here.

The good news for Taylor's RB2 value is Seth McGowan (hamstring) is "going to miss some time." Over the past month, McGowan has stolen real work from Taylor before garbage time. That's included some red-zone scores, and I totally get why they were doing that, as McGowan was running well. They'll stop rotating Taylor out now. Over the past month, Taylor has been the RB52 (!!!) on RB16 usage. We're back to having hope for an RB15 on RB10 usage finish.

The matchup is daunting. The Giants suffocate games on both sides with a balanced offense and a hard-hitting defense. They upset the Jaguars last week, holding Bhayshul Tuten to just 53 yards. Ditto to the Commanders RBs in Week 10 and Saquon Barkley in Week 9. On the whole, New York is averaging just 16.6 half PPR points to RB rooms (27th).

21. Ollie Gordon (vs. NYJ) - 89.5 proj. total yards

Gordon is the RB16 on RB18 usage since being the Dolphins' starter, but the wind is coming out of the sail right now. He's down to the RB41 on RB27 usage this month with the offense losing Malik Willis. He's been the RB18 and RB24 over the past two weeks with Kyle McCord, and one of those was a Colts' game. It'll be hard for Gordon to see 16+ carries if the Dolphins are trailing early.

The Jets rank ninth in half PPR points allowed to running backs at 21.9 points per game. New York has surrendered heavy production on the ground, ranking 8th in rushing points allowed to backs, and gave up an RB1 finish to Kenneth Walker III and an RB7 finish to James Cook over their last four games with DT T'Vondre Sweat on IR. Gordon posted 16.8 half PPR points on 25 carries against them back in Week 7. Miami enters as 3.5-point home underdogs with an implied team total of 18.5 points (26th).

22. Ashton Jeanty (at CLE) - 75.5 proj. total yards

Jeanty had his best fantasy outing since Week 1, based on two explosive plays. He went untouched for 46 yards up the gut when the LB and S got washed up, and then he ran a wheel route against part-time OLB Quandarrius Robinson for a long score. It's awesome that this happened, but if we're being honest, he had a lot of daylight on each of them.

The good news is he still had 15.8 expected half PPR points (RB10) with five receptions while splitting carries fairly evenly with Mike Washington Jr. Jeanty has come out of the absolute bottom of his workload and looks healthy. We'll see if he can create more plays down the stretch as a boom-bust fantasy RB2. He's the RB17 on RB11 usage this year now.

23. Quinshon Judkins (vs. LV) - 62.5 proj. total yards

Judkins is the RB23 on RB25 usage since pass-catching backup Dylan Sampson has returned to the lineup. Judkins' receiving role has been bad over the past month (1.8 receptions per game), so he's entirely touchdown dependent as a FLEX option. The good news is his workload is pretty stable, putting up between 10.7 and 12.6 expected half PPR points in five-straight games.

The Raiders rank 4th in half PPR points allowed to running backs, yielding 24.6 points per game. That vulnerability is almost entirely on the ground, where Las Vegas ranks 1st in rushing points allowed to backs (19.5 per game), compared to ranking 28th against receiving backs. That's okay for Judkins!!! Jonah Coleman (RB1) and Braelon Allen (RB7) each posted top-10 finishes against them recently. Cleveland sits as 4.5-point home favorites with an implied total of 23.0 points (15th).

24. Jaylen Warren (vs. DEN) - 78.5 proj. total yards

Last week was a nightmare game. There weren't many lanes on film review, and he couldn't bring in what could've been a 31-yard receiving TD on a ball that was a bit high on Aaron Rodgers. Beyond that, the Steelers were trailing, which meant Warren and Rico Dowdle combined for just five touches in the second half. Across the entire season, Warren is averaging 2.6 expected half PPR points fewer in games with Dowdle at this point, on 4.0 fewer carries and 1.2 fewer targets per game. Warren is back to being a firm fantasy RB2.

The matchup is one that comes with some advantages and some weaknesses. The Broncos have a strong DL, one that will put pressure on their backup LG. Denver also has very concerning LB play, while having standouts at all corner spots. The ball typically gets funneled to RBs against the Broncos, who are allowing the ninth-most fantasy points to the position on 126 rushing yards per game (10th). Ashton Jeanty popped up for 169 total yards last week, while Chuba Hubbard (96) and Emmett Johnson (143) hit them hard in the outings before that. The Steelers only project for 17.25 points (30th), so the lack of floor is alarming.

25. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (at ARI) - 61.5 proj. total yards

Croskey-Merritt returned from injury and was the Commanders' go-to option right away. They demoted Rachaad White to distant third duties, while Austin Ekeler spelled Bill. He ended up as the RB12 on RB17 usage in a close upset win. He handled the lone inside the five-yard line opportunity and offers the most juice on the ground. He can be phased out as a forgettable receiving option, but when the Commanders are rolling, he can get hot.

Well, Arizona up next! The Cardinals allow 20.8 half PPR points per game to running backs (12th-most), including 14.4 points per game specifically on the ground (13th). Arizona has surrendered big yardage and scoring on the ground recently, including Emmett Johnson (RB6) posting 105 rushing yards and a score in Week 11 and Blake Corum (RB9) gaining 100 yards and a touchdown in Week 10. Washington heads out as seven-point road favorites with a 23.75-point implied team total (13th).

26. Aaron Jones Sr. (vs. ATL) - 47.5 proj. total yards

Jones is only the RB45 on RB50 usage in 6 games with Jordan Mason, but Kirk Cousins is here to save the day. Over the past two weeks, Jones is the RB20 and RB19 on RB14 and RB35 usage. Cousins is willing to check the ball down, plus is going to sustain more drives than what Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz were able to do earlier on. Jones is still mixing in the occasion touchdown despite being the smaller back.

The Vikings are in a better spot this time around. They're touchdown favorites to the Falcons, who were smoked by Emmett Johnson last week (171 total yards). Bucky Irving (170) and Christian McCaffrey (100) were also top-10 backs against them this month. Across the entire season, Atlanta is allowing the 5th-most fantasy points to RBs. There is far more FLEX appeal this time around than in previous weeks. A 24.75-point team total (9th) backs that up.

27. David Montgomery (vs. BAL) - 54.5 proj. total yards

Montgomery is going back to a split backfield with Wood Marks expected to clear the concussion protocol, so we can largely through last week's predictable solid outing (RB13 on RB6 usage) against the tanking Colts. In Weeks 1-4 with Marks, Montgomery was the RB23 on RB30 usage. He lit up the Bills in Week 1, then was the RB47, RB36, and RB45 in the following games. I thought Marks was out-playing him on tape. After last week's clean outing, it'll be Monty as the starter and lead back most likely. Unfortunately, if it's somewhere around a 60/40 split, then it's harder to make the math work. The Texans' RB room is averaging 18.0 expected half PPR points, and their efficiency is almost always bad.

The good news is the Texans have found a grove on offense with C.J. Stroud throwing the ball well with a deep WR room. Houston owns a 26.5-point team total as big favorites to the struggling Ravens. Baltimore was gashed by Chuba Hubbard (RB2), Omarion Hampton (RB11), Chris Rodriguez (RB18) and James Cook (RB13) over the past month, leading to the 7th-most points over that span. Montgomery has fart into the end zone hope here. He's a solid FLEX.

28. Zach Charbonnet (at SF) - 71.5 proj. total yards

Charbonnet has been the RB39, RB22 and RB24 since returning from a torn ACL. He had the bye week to get his legs back under him, though that also plays into Post-Bye Rookie Bump Jadarian Price. They've split the workload in fairly predictable ways. Charbonnet is going to handle most of the goal-line and short-yardage carries, while Price is going to be designed a couple of targets and given some perimeter runs to take advantage of his better speed. The Seahawks are a balanced offense, so either one can have a random big game. For the most part, Charbonnet is not a big-play threat, so his role is far more touchdown-dependent.

The 49ers rank 25th in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields at 16.8 per game, presenting a split matchup profile. San Francisco has been stout against pure ground work, sitting 31st against RB rushing (8.6 points per game allowed), but ranks sixth-most favorable against RB receiving at 8.0 half PPR points per game. Bijan Robinson (RB19) managed five receptions for 59 yards against them in Week 7, while Ashton Jeanty (RB43) was limited to 25 rushing yards on six carries in Week 9. Seattle enters as three-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 22.25 points (16th).

29. Rhamondre Stevenson (at LAC) - 65.5 proj. total yards

The Patriots are turning to Tommy DeVito this week, immediately being faced with a 17.0-point team total (30th). It's fair to say full adjustments are needed, even if TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is on IR and may not play again this year. Stevenson was phased out of the game in Germany before this bye, but hopefully he's fresher now. He'll split time with early-down option Corey Kiner. The matchup is just fine. The Chargers are middle of the back in all defensive metrics.

Unfortunately, we're in the Wild West for Stevenson's fantasy value. He's at the mercy of just how bad the QB play will be moving forward. We're probably at the point where the savior is Daniel Jones in a week or so. Never a good spot to be in.

30. Kaleb Johnson (at LAR) - 35.5 proj. total yards

Josh Jacobs (finger) will miss, leaving the Packers with Johnson and Marshawn Lloyd on the ground, with Chris Brooks in for pass protection. To me, Johnson is just way better than Lloyd as a rusher. The Packers seem to agree. He was the one to lead the backfield in carries in Week 10 without Jacobs, and there's no reason to believe he won't see 10-15 carries off the bye. Johnson is the RB26 on RB40 usage since Week 9 while facing the Patriots and Vikings.

The Packers will be challenged by a Rams' veteran-filled DL fresh off the bye. Los Angeles is the second-best defense against fantasy RBs this year, completely shutting out bad run games of late (ARI, WAS, LAC, LV, ARI). James Cook III was able to post 118 total yards against them in Week 5, at least. Johnson is a red-zone threat for a team projected for 20.75 points on Thanksgiving. He's a half-PPR FLEX.

31. Travis Etienne Jr. (at CIN) - 66.5 proj. total yards

We'll need two more data centers to figure out how Etienne wasn't able to score on his 46-yard run last week:

Etienne disproving geometry theorems pic.twitter.com/47dYFVHtgY

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 23, 2026

I can't say his tape has looked very good since returning, but the Saints are at least committing to him on the ground with Audric Estimé healthy-scratched. Etienne was the RB23 on RB18 usage, ceding all receiving work to protector C.J. Donaldson and Alvin Kamara. That puts a firm lid on his fantasy value, especially while the OL has backups at C and RT. He'll need a TD to pay off as a FLEX play. Last week, Kamara subbed in for a designed receiving touchdown near the goal line.

32. Omarion Hampton (vs. NE) - 71.5 proj. total yards

Hampton had another solid game, as the Chargers were at least able to keep the game close. It's clear that when Hampton is in, they're going to call a bunch of pitches at this point. He took one for 36 yards off the edge this week. He's still not trusted in the passing game and lost plenty of snaps to Kimani Vidal this past week. Still, Hampton being the RB18 on RB25 usage is a win. Over the past month coming out of the bye, Hampton is the RB38 on RB33 usage. He's very game-script dependent.

33. Braelon Allen (at MIA) - 55.5 proj. total yards

34. Jordan Mason (vs. ATL) - 64.5 proj. total yards

35. Kyle Monangai (at DET) - 42.5 proj. total yards

Monangai only had eight carries in his return from turf toe. I went into his tape not knowing which foot had the injury, but after the first few carries, I was able to figure that out (and was correct after looking it up). His right side is bugging him, and it's coming through when he's trying to cut on it. Monangai is simply not near 100% health. He'll have a short week to get right for Thanksgiving, but that's asking for too much. It's more likely that the Bears keep him in a more part-time role. He was the RB32 in usage last week with six teams on bye as a forgettable FLEX option.

At least Monangai has a clean matchup with the Lions on deck. They've been very strong against fantasy RBs throughout the season, but they're without DE Aidan Hutchinson and LB Jack Campbell right now. Bucky Irving had 100 yards, plus an 80-yard score called back against them last week. The markets agree that it's a soft matchup, as Chicago has an impressive 29.0-point team total (third) on Thanksgiving. Hoping for a touchdown in this offense isn't the worst fantasy idea.

36. Samaje Perine (vs. NO)

Are we sure he's worse than Chase Brown? I view Perine as one of the best insurance backs in fantasy down the stretch. Add him now.

37. Jadarian Price (at SF) - 40.5 proj. total yards

38. Kenneth Gainwell (vs. CAR) - 37.5 proj. total yards

39. Rico Dowdle (vs. DEN) - 40.5 proj. total yards

40. Alvin Kamara (at CIN)

41. Mike Washington (at CLE)

42. Dylan Sampson (vs. LV) - 47.5 proj. total yards

43. Woody Marks (vs. BAL)

44. Tyler Allgeier (vs. WAS)

45. Austin Ekeler (at ARI)

46. Justice Hill (at HOU)

47. Kaelon Black (vs. SEA) - 33.5 proj. total yards

48. Corey Kiner (at LAC) - 29.5 proj. total yards

item.title: Chuck Clark, DJ Wonnum are inactive for the Lions
item.description: The Lions will be missing a pair of defensive starters for Thursday's home game against the Bears.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions will be missing a pair of defensive starters for Thursday's home game against the Bears.

Safety Chuck Clark and defensive end DJ Wonnum are both inactive after being listed as questionable to play on the team's final injury report. Clark has a hamstring injury and Wonnum has a back injury.

Clark's absence could lead to more playing time for Kerby Joseph, who will be playing his second game since being activated from the physically unable to perform list. The Lions will also be getting cornerback D.J. Reed back after he missed three games with a hip injury.

Cornerback Ennis Rakestraw, defensive back Keith Abney, and defensive end Tyrus Wheat are also inactive for Detroit.

The Bears have deactivated quarterback Case Keenum, cornerback Kyler Gordon, cornerback Isaac Yiadom, defensive back Elijah Hicks, running back Roschon Johnson, offensive lineman Jordan McFadden, and defensive lineman Jayden Loving.

item.title: Lions Week 12 inactives: DJ Wonnum, Chuck Clark OUT vs. Bears
item.description: The Detroit Lions have released their inactives ahead of Week 12 matchup with the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving Day.
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions have declared their inactives ahead of their Week 12, Thanksgiving Day matchup with the Chicago Bears, and the Lions have ruled two of their defensive starters, DJ Wonnum and Chuck Clark, OUT for this game.

Both were able to get in a limited practice on Wednesday, but on a short week, they didn’t have enough time to heal up ahead of this game. With Wonnum out, the Lions will need rookie Derrick Moore to level up his game again, as well as getting contributions from Tyler Lacy, Ahmed Hassanein, and others to rotate on the opposite side. With no Clark, the Lions will shift Brian Branch into a safety-only role, and elevate Kerby Joseph snaps. Look for the Lions to shift back to their corner rotation to cover their nickel duties.

If you missed this week’s roster transactions or need a refresher, we’ve got you covered with an updated depth chart, position-by-position rankings, and a visual overview. We also delivered a plethora of game previews leading up to this game, including my breakdowns of the Bears’ offensive/defensive schemes and Honolulu Blueprint: Predictions for a victory, an On Paper preview from Jeremy Reisman, 5 questions with a Bears writer from Ryan Mathews, 4 key stats to know from Al Karsten, our POD staff pick-em predictions from Brandon Knapp, and our fans pick-a-winner survey results.

With the Lions placing Skyler Gill-Howard on injured reserve, their active roster has been reduced to 52 players. However, they also elevated one practice squad player for this game (edge rusher Anthony Lucas), bringing their game-day roster to 53 players. With 48 players eligible to play, Detroit needs to declare five players inactive for today’s matchup.

Lions inactives:

  • EDGE DJ Wonnum (back)
  • EDGE Tyrus Wheat
  • CB Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder) — Ruled OUT on Wednesday
  • DB Keith Abney
  • S Chuck Clark (hamstring)

Bears inactives:

  • RB Roschon Johnson (ankle) — Ruled OUT on Wednesday
  • CB Kyler Gordon (shoulder) — Ruled OUT on Wednesday
  • S Elijah Hicks (concussion) — Ruled OUT on Wednesday
  • OL Jordan McFadden
  • DB Isaac Yiadom
  • DT Jayden Loving
  • QB Case Keenum (emergency No. 3 QB)
